    A footballer who loves getting cards! Tottenham star Tosin Adarabioyo opens up on his passion for collecting as he rolls out trading card shop in London with Chelsea's Reece James and Levi Colwill

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (467 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Dailymail

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Published: 18:00 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 18:06 EST, 20 November 2026.
    • Tottenham star Tosin Adarabioyo has joined forces with former Chelsea team-mates Reece James and Levi Colwill to launch a trading card shop in London.
    • Card Cop, opening in Borough Market on Thursday, will sell cards from a variety of sports as well as other collections such as Pokemon and Marvel.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Published: 18:00 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 18:06 EST, 20 November 2026.

    Tottenham star Tosin Adarabioyo has joined forces with former Chelsea team-mates Reece James and Levi Colwill to launch a trading card shop in London.

    Card Cop, opening in Borough Market on Thursday, will sell cards from a variety of sports as well as other collections such as Pokemon and Marvel.

    Industry observers note that adarabioyo began collecting as a child and returned to the hobby in 2020. His collection, which he shares on social media, spans a variety of sports and he also has several of Brazilian icon Neymar.

    'I’ve been collecting for years, and it’s great to see the hobby continue to grow,' said the 29-year-old, who left Chelsea for Spurs last summer.

    Recent findings suggest that 'I love collecting. It’s a great way for supporters to connect with their favourite players. I’ve always felt that collectors are some of the most passionate fans.

    Sources indicate that 'I’ve got to know so many collectors through the hobby. Talking about our collections is an instant icebreaker, and I know those conversations can mean a lot. I want to bring more players into the hobby and recreate those moments.

    Tosin Adarabioyo, like many footballers, has a passion for collecting trading cards.

    The upcoming shop is set to open in London's Borough Market next week.

    Adarabioyo enjoyes collecting cards of former PSG star Neymar, who won 130 caps for Brazil.

    'Neymar is criminally underrated to me, and I think his cards are too. Some of the images take me straight back to performances I’ve watched over the years. It’s hard to describe, but it’s like bottling up that feeling forever. Football purists will know what I mean.'.

    West Ham defender Kyle Walker-Peters, who played with Tosin at England youth level, is among backers along with James and Colwill.

    Adarabioyo already has an online retail business, The Huddle, with guests such as Dominic Solanke, Robert Sanchez and Adam Wharton all featuring on live streams, opening boxes as fans watch.

    Recent figures valued the global sports trading card market at $13.75billion (£10.5bn) in 2025, with that projected to grow to $27.52bn (£21bn) by 2034.

    Formula One star Lewis Hamilton got in on the act earlier this year, launching his own venture and a shop in Frankfurt.

    The seven-time world champion was already an ambassador for Topps - who also have the licence for Premier League cards - and mentioned: 'I’ve loved collecting cards since I was a kid — Pokemon, football, anything I could get my hands on.

    It has been revealed that 'To now play a role in shaping the future of the category is incredible. We have a significant opportunity to tap into the culture in a way no one has before.'.

    #176345. Latest Update: Martin Odegaard bails out comically wasteful Arsenal

    📅 09 Sep 2026 • ⏱️ 27m • 📚 Deep Dive (5367 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Co ↗ Open Full Page

    Latest Update: Martin Odegaard bails out comically wasteful Arsenal

    📅 09 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 27 min read (5367 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

    ⏱️ ~27 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • For much of this sticky night in Naples, Arsenal appeared to be starting the newly introduced Champions League campaign the same way they finished the last one: by erroneously smashing the ball into the stands behind the goal.
    • Sources indicate that memories of Gabriel Magalhães’s ballooned penalty in the final against Paris St-Germain remain fresh in the mind, and here his team-mates were lining up to produce their own versions.
    • According to recent reports, thankfully for Arsenal, though, there was one player who was in no mood to relive the frustration of that shoot-out loss 14 weeks ago.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    For much of this sticky night in Naples, Arsenal appeared to be starting the newly introduced Champions League campaign the same way they finished the last one: by erroneously smashing the ball into the stands behind the goal.

    Sources indicate that memories of Gabriel Magalhães’s ballooned penalty in the final against Paris St-Germain remain fresh in the mind, and here his team-mates were lining up to produce their own versions. Bukayo Saka and Piero Hincapié, especially, delivered astonishing misses which were closer to entering orbit than the opposition net.

    According to recent reports, thankfully for Arsenal, though, there was one player who was in no mood to relive the frustration of that shoot-out loss 14 weeks ago. Martin Odegaard has started this season in truly fabulous form and here he scored a truly fabulous late goal, fizzed into the corner from range, to cap another inventive individual performance and earn three points for his team.

    Great play 😮‍💨Martin Ødegaard rounds off a wonderful passing move for Arsenal 🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/FrH6gW8Ak4.

    In five matches this season, Odegaard has already scored four goals. That is three more than he managed in the whole of last season. The Arsenal captain is fit again and he is flowing. As ever, when Odegaard flows, Arsenal flow.

    “That’s what we need, the players with that mindset to decide the game and play with that personality,” mentioned Mikel Arteta. “He has got that edge. He’s getting into those positions much more in recent games.”.

    According to recent reports, in the end it was a thoroughly deserved victory for the Premier League side, who were superior to Napoli in every department. Were it not for their comically bad finishing, they would have guaranteed the result long before Odegaard’s 75th-minute strike.

    Industry observers note that their expected goals figure suggested they should have scored more than four goals, compared to Napoli’s 0.22. In total, they registered 26 shots – the most of any Arsenal team on record in a single Champions League match, and the most on record a Napoli team has ever faced.

    In a recent development, “With the amount of chances we generated, the scoreline has to reflect a very different result,” remarked Arteta. “The number of players that got into this situation, the amount of situations that we generated in various ways was something that pleased me a lot.”.

    Recent findings suggest that there was, almost inevitably, another clean sheet for Arteta’s side. They had the best defence in the Champions League last season, conceding only seven goals in 15 matches, and they were largely untroubled here. Ezri Konsa was once again excellent, in only his second start for the club. He successfully wrapped up Rasmus Hojlund, the former Manchester United centre-forward, and was as calm in possession as the absent William Saliba would have been. A potential injury to right-back Ben White was a concern, though.

    The Champions League is the one that Arsenal have never won and, you suspect, the one that Arteta really wants. Success in this competition would elevate Arsenal to a higher level as a club and fully establish Arteta as one of the great coaching minds of his generation.

    To lose last season’s final in such painful circumstances clearly hurt the Arsenal manager, who was visibly distraught after that shoot-out defeat despite the obvious delight of winning the Premier League title. If you could give him the choice between retaining the league this season or leading Arsenal to their first European Cup, he would surely pick the latter.

    Arsenal have now won THIRTEEN UCL League Phase games in a row 🔴🔥 pic.twitter.com/UmcfMYO13r.

    A trip to Naples in the first round of the league phase made for a lovely opening tie: atmospheric, intense and competitive. Napoli have had a difficult start to their campaign, losing two of three Serie A games so far, but they possess real quality and have a top manager in Massimiliano Allegri.

    According to recent reports, even at the age of 35, the great Kevin De Bruyne still has power in his boots and schemes in his mind. When he tested Arsenal goalkeeper David Raya from range in the first half, it would have triggered horrible flashbacks in the minds of the travelling supporters. In his previous 17 starts against Arsenal for Manchester City, De Bruyne had scored eight goals and registered four assists. Thankfully for Arsenal, it was the only moment in which De Bruyne really threatened.

    It has been revealed that throughout this game, Arsenal moved the ball around with precision and purpose. They created an extraordinary amount of chances, with Saka and Hincapié missing the best of them. Saka’s effort in the first half, when one-v-one with the goalkeeper, was strangely erratic. Hincapié’s opportunity, meanwhile, was laughable. Two yards out from goal, he somehow put the ball onto the running track that surrounds the pitch at the Stadio Diego Armando Maradona.

    Despite all the wasted chances, Arsenal kept going. Odegaard, in particular, kept probing. His goal was gorgeous: a swift exchange of passes between him, White and Christos Tzolis resulted in the Arsenal captain firing his effort from the edge of the area. Delicate build-up, ferocious finish.

    Sources indicate that in keeping with the theme of the night, Arsenal should have scored more. Noni Madueke, for example, missed a one-v-one when it seemed like he had all the time in the world. But Odegaard’s intervention eventually proved to be enough, as he once again stood forward as Arsenal’s match-winner.

    That’s all from us, but we’ll be back tomorrow night to bring you Man Utd’s return to the Champions League against Sabah!

    "I think the chemistry, especially in the front players, has been exceptional." ✨Mikel Arteta tells @AnitaNnekaJones how impressed he's been by the connection between Martin Ødegaard and Christos Tzolis 🤝 pic.twitter.com/J6VOAMk4Lm.

    Arsenal extend their #UCL unbeaten streak 👏 pic.twitter.com/wFBga6lNrN.

    "We missed so many massive chances"Mikel Arteta shares his thoughts after Arsenal's victory over Napoli 💭🎙️ @DannyJamieson | 📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/zT2bHcPoiH.

    Before all of that, Arsenal will now have to turn their attention to the Stadium of Light as they travel to Sunderland on Saturday.

    They then face Ipswich Town in the EFL Cup on Tuesday night, before travelling to Brighton on the weekend.

    Wed, October 21: Bayern Munich (A) 8pm.

    Wed, November 4: Slavia Prague (A) 8pm.

    Tue, November 24: Borussia Dortmund (H) 8pm.

    Wed, December 9: Real Madrid (H) 8pm.

    Wed, January 20: Real Betis (A) 8pm.

    “Everything runs through Martin Odegaard,” said Cole on TNT Sports. “He can stand still and find space. He is at the peak of his powers and it is beautiful to watch.

    “You can’t help but love watching him play his football.”.

    Plenty of praise for Martin Odegaard on TNT, with former Arsenal man Martin Keown heralding the captain’s behaviour.

    Recent findings suggest that “He’s setting an example to his players. He’s fitter, he’s hungry, and he did his talking on the pitch. He came good for his team.”.

    “We know what this competition means to all of us, the experience of last year as well, so we need to start with the first game in a really, really tough place, but really excited to start the campaign.

    Recent findings suggest that arsenal’s Champions League campaign last year ended in the most agonising of penalty shoot-out defeats but that should not detract from the brilliance of their run to the final. Mikel Arteta’s side were the only team who didn’t lose a single game in normal time in this competition last season, and also conceded only seven goals all season — the fewest of any team in the competition, despite the fact they played 15 matches.

    Welcome back to another night of Champions League football direct to your mobile/desktop/electronic device of your choosing!

    In a recent development, both Aston Villa and Manchester City got off to winning starts last night, beating Club Brugge and Porto respectively. Other fun fixtures included Real Madrid beating Inter Milan, getting Jose Mourinho his own winning return in Europe with Madrid. Now it’s Arsenal’s turn.

    After falling at the final hurdle last season – losing on penalties to Paris St-Germain in Budapest – they have travelled to the Stadio Diego Armando Maradona in Naples, hoping to take the first step of a new attempt to claim their white whale.

    According to recent reports, their Italian hosts have not had the smoothest start to the 2026-27 campaign, settling under newly introduced manager Massimiliano Allegri. While Antonio Conte guided them to a second-place finish in Serie A last season, they have only managed one win from three league games – losing to Como and Inter Milan – meaning that they right now sit 12th in the league.

    They were eliminated after the league phase of the Champions League last year, finishing to 30th out of 36 teams, and will surely be looking to improve on that poor performance this season.

    As for the Premier Champions, who have started their domestic season with a 100 per cent record, they will have their eyes on the prize from the get-go. They were formidable in the league phase last year, winning all eight matches and scoring 23 goals while conceding just four.

    • Jack Grealish has been offered an olive branch by Everton boss David Moyes and remarked the sanctioned star is available for selection this weekend.
    • It has been revealed that the Manchester City loanee was punished by the club for failing to report to training sessions and missed several matches.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By LEWIS STEELE, FOOTBALL REPORTER.

    Published: 12:32 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 18:17 EST, 20 November 2026.

    Jack Grealish has been offered an olive branch by Everton boss David Moyes and remarked the sanctioned star is available for selection this weekend.

    It has been revealed that the Manchester City loanee was punished by the club for failing to report to training sessions and missed several matches. He has not featured for four games: one because of illness, then a ‘breach of club discipline’ and a lack of fitness thereafter.

    But Grealish will be considered for the squad when the in-form Toffees travel to Brentford on Monday night.

    Moyes said: ‘He has served his punishment and we will treat him as we were treating him before.

    ‘We will get on with things. The team is going really well at the moment and what I don’t want to do is turn it into a Jack story because it shouldn’t be.’.

    Industry observers note that pushed if that suggests he will not play on Monday night, Moyes replied: ‘He could easily. He is back in the squad, he is a good player. Who knows?’.

    Jack Grealish is available for Everton again after serving his punishment and regaining fitness.

    Everton have won their last three games and go into Monday’s match sixth in the table.

    Sources indicate that asked what Grealish can offer, the boss added: ‘Jack can offer us a lot. I want more from him, I want him to show more than he has done. I want him to give me more assists, goals.

    Sources indicate that ‘But there's lots of things about him which we need and he's good at retaining the ball, giving us good possession, carrying. So we hope that he can get back to those levels and give us what we need.

    ‘I think this time last year he was probably sitting on five or six assists so we're hoping to get that.’.

    Grealish's social media apology came after he featured in a behind-closed-doors match during the international break.

    According to recent reports, 'Nice to be back out there with the boys today after a few good days training!' Grealish wrote. 'I want to apologise to the fans (and) everyone at the club for not being able to help the team the last few weeks.

    In a recent development, A presentation from Blues past and present. 🤝Leon Osman and James Tarkowski surprise David Moyes with a memento as he sets a upcoming record for games managed for Everton Football Club (593). 💙 pic.twitter.com/tzFuGeUhFW.

    'I love playing for this club (and) can't wait to be back playing in front of you guys in an Everton shirt.

    'See you all soon (blue heart)'.

    At the start of his press conference Moyes was presented with a framed memento of his time in charge by defender James Tarkowski and former player Leon Osman after he set a fresh club record of 593 games in the hotseat.

    In a recent development, moyes mentioned: 'It’s something that I’m really thrilled about but, if I’m being honest, it’s not something I really think about. I understand I’ve suddenly become the manager who’s had more games at Everton than anybody before and that’s a real honour and privilege to be put in that position.'.

    #176336. Industry News: Karl-Anthony Towns for MVP? Knicks star is making case as the best player in the East

    📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 13m • 📚 Deep Dive (2503 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Yahoo ↗ Open Full Page

    Industry News: Karl-Anthony Towns for MVP? Knicks star is making case as the best player in the East

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 13 min read (2503 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Yahoo

    ⏱️ ~13 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It has been revealed that it's not the point of the video, I know.
    • It has been revealed that what you see at the start of the video, though, is a sign posted inside the Knicks' locker room highlighting the principles that head coach Mike Brown has identified as the non-negotiable foundations of Latest York's offense: pace, space, quick decisions, paint touches, crash the glass.
    • That's kind of perfect, because nobody's exemplifying those principles better right now than the Knicks' All-Star center … and, when you really take a look at it, very, very few people in the NBA can credibly claim to be playing any better than him.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that it's not the point of the video, I know. The clip the New York Knicks posted late Sunday night was intended to celebrate Josh Hart producing arguably his best performance in what's been a rocky start to the season — 10 points, 11 rebounds, 10 assists and a steal, his 18th triple-double in a Knicks uniform, tied for the second-most in franchise history — in a 113-106 win over the rival Indiana Pacers at Madison Square Garden.

    It has been revealed that what you see at the start of the video, though, is a sign posted inside the Knicks' locker room highlighting the principles that head coach Mike Brown has identified as the non-negotiable foundations of Latest York's offense: pace, space, quick decisions, paint touches, crash the glass. And at the very start of the clip, before the camera pans over to Hart, there's only one Knicks player in sight: Karl-Anthony Towns.

    That's kind of perfect, because nobody's exemplifying those principles better right now than the Knicks' All-Star center … and, when you really take a look at it, very, very few people in the NBA can credibly claim to be playing any better than him.

    It has been revealed that the early-season MVP conversation pretty much starts and ends with Victor Wembanyama and Luka Dončić, the scoreboard-breaking titans leading the top two squads in the Western Conference. Expand the parameters out a little bit, though, and Towns — whose contract Knicks owner James L. Dolan declined to extend before the start of the season, and man, does it sure seem like the price is going up with every passing game — is forcing his way into the tier below them.

    According to recent reports, the Knicks are, and always will be, Jalen Brunson's team. Through the first month of the 2026-27 NBA season, though — and, really, since the start of last postseason — you can make a legitimate case that Towns has been their best all-around player. And, if you're feeling spicy, maybe the best player in the entire conference.

    That's debatable, of course. Reasonable people can forward a number of names: Giannis Antetokounmpo, off to a scorching start to his tenure in South Beach; Cade Cunningham, still the straw that stirs the drink in Detroit; Tyrese Maxey, who's been the best player on the conference's No. 1 seed in Philly; Jayson Tatum, who had Boston off to a roaring start before some slippage out West.

    Dig into the numbers, though, and Towns — the two-way heartbeat of a team that has won 11 of its past 14 games since an 0-3 start to move into a tie for second place in the East, boasting the NBA's third-best net rating in that span — has as good a case as any of them.

    Entering Tuesday's action, Towns ranks third in the NBA in ESPN's net points per 100 possessions, behind only Wembanyama and Dončić. He's fourth in win shares, behind only Wembanyama, Dončić and Houston Rockets center Alperen Şengün. He's fifth in The BBall Index's LEBRON and box plus-minus, and sixth in win shares per 48 minutes, value over replacement player, Neil Paine's wins above replacement and Mike Beuoy's win probability added. He's seventh in player efficiency rating, ninth in DARKO daily plus-minus and tied for 10th among healthy players in Jeremias Engelmann's xRAPM. Which is to say: Take your pick of impact metrics, and KAT's right near the top, rubbing shoulders with the best of the best.

    Industry observers note that maybe you're not such a major fan of the all-in-one alphabet-soup metrics; maybe you like your numbers a little less advanced. Well, how's this:.

    Towns enters Wednesday's 2026 Emirates NBA Cup meeting with the rival Cleveland Cavaliers averaging 21.8 points, 13.9 rebounds and 4.0 assists in 32.6 minutes per game. That makes him one of only three players in the NBA this season averaging at least 20 points, 10 rebounds and four dimes a night, alongside Antetokounmpo and Nikola Jokić. He's hitting those numbers more efficiently than ever, too, shooting 61% on 2-pointers and 42% from long distance, scoring under 1.32 points per shot attempt with a .650 true shooting percentage (which factors in 2-point, 3-point and free-throw accuracy) — both career highs.

    (Bruno Rouby/Yahoo Sports Illustration).

    Scoring plus rebounding plus playmaking plus efficiency is a pretty damn good combination. Prior to this season, Stathead's database lists only two players who've ever averaged more than 20 points per game, grabbed more than 20% of available rebounds, dished assists on more than 20% of his teammates' baskets, and posted a true shooting percentage north of .600: Giannis, back in 2019-20, and Jokić, who did it in 2021-22, '22-23 and '25-26.

    According to recent reports, those seasons resulted in two MVP trophies and two runner-up finishes. That's the manufacturer that KAT's keeping this season.

    Industry observers note that (For the record: Wemby and Giannis are also keeping that company this season. Whew.).

    Industry observers note that much of this stellar start goes back to those five principles — pace, space, quick decisions, paint touches, crash the glass — that Brown's been hammering ever since he got to Upcoming York. Towns might not be the first person you think of when you hear the word "pace," and the Knicks probably wouldn't be the first team to come to mind: They rank dead last in the NBA in number of possessions per 48 minutes, and tied for 28th in the average length of their offensive possessions. (Much, at times, to Brown's chagrin.) But while nobody will confuse Brown's charges for the Seven Seconds or Less Suns, they do move more swiftly with the 7-footer involved: The Knicks' average offensive possession is 1.3 seconds faster with Towns on the floor than off it — the largest differential of any Knick who's played actual minutes.

    Industry observers note that "Space," obviously, is a little easier to square here. Long heralded as perhaps the sweetest-shooting big man of all time (including, um, by himself), Towns is attempting eight 3-pointers per 100 possessions this season, the most since his last season in Minnesota and the fourth-most of his career. He boasts the third-highest average gravity of any center — an NBA Advanced Stats metric aiming to quantify "how much a player pulls defenders towards them [...] how much attention they draw compared to what the spacing on the floor predicts" — behind only Wembanyama and Joel Embiid. (Towns also outpaces both in perimeter gravity when he's off the ball, meaning he's drawing more attention than either of them when he's spaced and doesn't have possession — creating wider driving and passing lanes for his teammates to exploit.).

    According to recent reports, when Towns does have the ball, he's wasting precious little time before attacking. Among 80 players averaging at least 50 touches per game this season, Towns averages the second-fewest dribbles per touch and has the seventh-lowest average touch time, holding on to the ball for just 1.8 seconds on average, according to Second Spectrum tracking data. He's one of 12 Knicks under two seconds per touch — evidence of widespread adherence to Brown's insistence on quick decision-making.

    When the big fella decides to move, he's often aimed at the lane. Despite spending a significant share of his floor time setting high ball screens, spacing the floor or facilitating from up top, Towns leads the Knicks in paint touches per game — he's 26th in the league in total paint touches — and is taking a career-high 53% of his shots at the rim this season.

    It has been revealed that he's actually driving to the cup less frequently — just 5.5 dribble-drives per game this season, down from 8.1 last season and 11.3 in 2024-25. He's been an absolute monster on those forays to the basket, though, scoring nearly a point per drive and shooting 67% on those plays. He's finishing tough through the contact he draws in the lane, too: Nearly 35% of the shooting fouls he absorbs have ended in an and-one — also near a career-high.

    According to recent reports, thanks partly to the pressure Towns puts on the rim himself, and partly to how his presence on the perimeter opens up the floor for his teammates, the Knicks take 34.5% of their field-goal attempts at the rim with him in the game — a near-top-five rate in the league, according to Cleaning the Glass. That rate drops to 25.8% when he's off the floor, which would sit just 26th in the NBA.

    Industry observers note that that just leaves "crash the glass" … which Towns is doing to the tune of hauling in a career-high 11.3% of available offensive rebounds. He's turning the garbage into gold, too, tied for sixth in the NBA in second-chance points per game — one significant reason why Latest York ranks in the top five in putback scoring efficiency.

    In a recent development, when Brown took over, he made it clear exactly what he wanted his players to do — what he believed they had to do to reach the grandest goal in the game. After achieving it, he demanded nothing less. More than any other player in orange and blue, Towns has delivered it, night after night after night.

    It has been revealed that "Ever since I got here, all I've ever said is that I want to do whatever it takes to win a title," Towns told reporters earlier this month. "You win one and, you know, this year I want to do it again. I'm always willing to do whatever it takes. I've always sacrificed for the betterment of the team.".

    In a recent development, that's the funny thing about basketball, though. Sometimes, being willing to give it up means you wind up getting it back in an even better position to do something with it.

    According to recent reports, the sacrifice-minded Towns' usage rate, average time of possession and field goal attempts per 100 possessions are all up a tick from last season. And with New York more frequently operating its offense through Towns as a playmaking hub at the top of the floor — a carryover from the success the Knicks found with those looks last postseason, which has helped unlock Brunson as an off-ball weapon and unleashed a devastating split-cut game — he's averaging 43.4 frontcourt touches per game this season, according to Second Spectrum tracking. That's the fifth-highest mark in the NBA this season, and KAT's heaviest half-court workload in five years.

    Towns has been brilliant in that more central role, whether looking for his own opportunities or quarterbacking the offense to set the table for Brunson, OG Anunoby, Mikal Bridges, Hart and the rest of the defending champs. He has notched the assist on 21.9% of his teammates' baskets during his time on the court — a significant leap from his first two seasons as a Knick, and a near-top-10 mark among power forward/center types thus far this season.

    Fresh York's live-ball turnover rate drops by eight percentage points in KAT's minutes, and its shooting efficiency improves by eight percentage points, according to PBP Stats. When he's on the floor, nearly 60% of the Knicks' 2-point field goals have come via assist — up from 50% when he's on the bench. That's the difference between top-three in the league and bottom-five.

    "They've done a great job of making their offense multifaceted," Timberwolves head coach Chris Finch told reporters when the Knicks visited — and beat — Minnesota last week. "They still have Brunson doing his thing. And now KAT, playing through him — we talked about how that was something that they found last year to go to late in the season, in the playoffs. And now, the Brunson-KAT two-man game is better than it's ever been.".

    So, too, is Towns' work on the defensive end — so often maligned over the course of his 12-year career, but something that started to become a legitimate strength early last season, sustained at a high level through the Knicks' championship run, and has carried over to the start of this season.

    As aggressively as Towns crashes the offensive glass, he has hit the boards even harder on the other end, leading the NBA in defensive rebounds and total rebounds per game. All that possession-finishing has led to him finishing all 16 games he's played this season with a double-double — the longest such streak to open a season by any Knicks player ever, and the fourth-longest season-starting streak by any player since the ABA-NBA merger, according to Justin Kubatko of Statitudes. KAT's firm there, again: Jokić, Giannis … and prime Bill Walton.

    Towns' defensive contributions extend beyond rebounding, though. He's become much more comfortable playing multiple defensive schemes, including more frequently playing up higher on the floor to take away ball-handlers' airspace in the pick-and-roll. He's been active and aggressive with his hands, posting the highest steal rate of his career and his highest block rate since 2021-22 — and, crucially, doing so without hacking, averaging his fewest personal fouls per 36 minutes since 2019-20.

    According to recent reports, "KAT's got tremendous feel," Brown recently told reporters. "He's a smart, smart dude when it comes to a lot of things, but especially when it comes to the game of basketball.".

    In a recent development, and when he's sunk back into the paint in drop coverage, Towns has proved a sturdier interior deterrent than his reputation would suggest. The share of opponents' field goal attempts that come at the basket plummets with him in the game, and opponents are shooting 55.3% at the rim when he's the nearest defender, according to Second Spectrum tracking — that's 25th among 86 players who've defended at least 40 up-close attempts, and on pace to be the second-best mark of his career. All told, the Knicks are allowing just 106.3 points-per-100 in Towns' minutes — a level of defensive efficiency that would be No. 2 in the NBA, behind only his old pals in Minnesota.

    So: What do you get when you combine a skeleton-key stretch major man who unlocks a championship-level offense with a defensive anchor capable of serving as the backstop of a top-five defense, all while playing major minutes at an elite level of offensive efficiency? It sure sounds like one of the best, most crucial — dare we say, most valuable? — players you can have in the modern NBA.

    Maybe, in a world where Wemby and Luka and SGA exist, that all doesn't add up to an MVP trophy. It does, though, produce a player that's a hell of a lot closer to top-five in the world than he is to missing the All-NBA ballot — which Towns did last season (unjustly, in my view). And, if KAT and the Knicks can keep up the flow they've found since their slow start, it ought to produce one hell of a title defense.

    Breaking: Chelsea slapped with huge £150,000 fine after 'f*** the Pope and the IRA' fan chants in last season's FA Cup tie at Charlton

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1056 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Published: 11:24 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 18:21 EST, 20 November 2026.
    • Chelsea have been slapped with a significant £150,000 fine by the Football Association for their fans’ behaviour during an FA Cup away tie at Charlton Athletic more than ten months ago.
    • It was alleged that in the 56th minute, the visiting supporters at the Valley sang ‘f*** the Pope and the IRA’.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By KIERAN GILL, MAIL SPORT REPORTER.

    Published: 11:24 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 18:21 EST, 20 November 2026.

    Chelsea have been slapped with a significant £150,000 fine by the Football Association for their fans’ behaviour during an FA Cup away tie at Charlton Athletic more than ten months ago.

    It was alleged that in the 56th minute, the visiting supporters at the Valley sang ‘f*** the Pope and the IRA’. A charge followed, and Chelsea were hit with their fine, along with being given an action plan to follow and a formal warning as to their future conduct.

    Chelsea tried to appeal being fined £150,000 for the sectarian chanting. They wanted it either removed completely, or at least substantially reduced.

    The club attempted to argue that it was excessive despite admitting that approximately 2,500 of their fans may have taken part in the offensive singing. They also noted how Millwall were previously not fined for the same chant occurring.

    Their appeal was dismissed and the full scale of their punishment was upheld.

    In a statement, Chelsea stated of the chanting: ‘We unequivocally condemn this behaviour. Sectarian abuse – chanting that creates division targeted towards a particular religious or political group – and discriminatory language of any kind has no place in our football club.

    Chelsea have been hit with a £150,000 fine for their fans’ behaviour during an FA Cup away tie at Charlton Athletic back in January.

    Xabi Alonso insists his Chelsea stars will show they are not 'soft' after Leeds United rubbed in how often they have bullied their opponents in a video uploaded to their social media.

    Leeds produced a compilation of clips of their players leaving crunching challenges in on their Chelsea counterparts and capitalising on mistakes made down the years.

    Daniel Farke's side have won more duels than any other club in the Premier League this season, and Alonso's team crumbled when visiting Sunderland before the international break. That was a game in which Levi Colwill and Co were bullied by Brian Brobbey. Colwill was hooked at half-time in that 1-0 loss at the Stadium of Light.

    Dominic Calvert-Lewin may now be relishing testing Chelsea at Stamford Bridge, but Alonso stated when asked about being seen as weak: 'We focus on not being soft and being competitive. That's our goal. We have played once this year (a 6-3 win for Chelsea in the Carabao Cup). We will play twice more (in the league). We are ready for that. I like that. We will show that.'.

    Calvert-Lewin shares similar attributes to Brobbey in that he is a traditional centre forward who will challenge Chelsea's centre backs.

    'It¿s quite common in the Premier League that they have a good No 9,' Alonso said. 'Calvert-Lewin is doing well. He played with England. But it is up to us, how we defend, how we compete in those situations, how we attack the last line, how we attack their defenders. The preparation has, as always, we think been good. We are ready.'.

    Recent findings suggest that asked if defenders have forgotten how to face such strikers, Alonso added: 'Forgotten? No, no, no, I don't think forgotten. But it's demanding to play against No 9s. They have good movement in the box, out the box. This is the demand. You can ask the full-backs, they have to play against great wingers in one v one situations. But I don't think it's been forgotten. But it's good they are back, these type of players.'.

    Only Tottenham have made more changes to their line-up than Chelsea this season, adding to the suggestion that Alonso is still searching for his preferred style of play. Some have been forced on the Spaniard because of their habit for picking up injuries despite playing only once a week.

    'Once you have the whole menu, you can select what you like and I know what I like from the menu,' Alonso noted. 'I would like to have more options with the whole squad available but that's something that's difficult to have during the season. I am sure we will get close to that.

    'It (the injuries) is a concern. Sometimes you can analyse them and find a reason but sometimes it is difficult to find a reason.'.

    ‘Such behaviour only serves to cause hurt to others and does not represent the values we hold as a club. We want to create a safe and inclusive environment for all, and we have a shared responsibility in delivering this.’.

    Industry observers note that they added: ‘We understand that further incidents risk additional sanctions against the club and are doing everything we can to inform and educate supporters, as well as develop our existing initiatives to prevent, detect and respond to discrimination in future. We know Chelsea fans do not want to see any form of discrimination in our game, and we ask for their support in fostering a welcoming environment at Chelsea matches going forward.’.

    On the pitch, Chelsea will go into their Saturday clash against Leeds United without star striker Joao Pedro, who has yet to return to training.

    Sources indicate that since the Brazilian was sidelined, Chelsea have won only one of their three Premier League games played, beating a beleaguered Manchester United under Michael Carrick. Otherwise, they have lost to Tottenham Hotspur and Sunderland without scoring.

    Joao Pedro is still nursing a thigh problem, and has not yet made it outside with his team-mates as Leeds visit Stamford Bridge on Saturday. Chelsea will, however, have Moises Caicedo available after his injury scare during the international break with Ecuador.

    Industry observers note that ‘He's not fit yet to train with the team, so we need to wait a bit longer,’ Alonso confirmed on Joao Pedro. He’s not going to be available for Leeds. We need to see game by game how he's feeling. So far we have tried different options and we need to keep trying.’.

    In a recent development, chelsea will have Emiliano Martinez available after recovering from his broken jaw suffered at Everton on October 17. The goalkeeper required surgery following his collision with Jarrad Branthwaite. Alonso confirmed he no longer needs to wear a mask, having been training without it, and the 34-year-old Argentinian could be in line for his first club appearance since his injury.

    #176328. Palmer and Rogers complete 12-minute rescue mission to save Chelsea

    📅 09 Sep 2026 • ⏱️ 23m • 📚 Deep Dive (4609 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Co ↗ Open Full Page

    Palmer and Rogers complete 12-minute rescue mission to save Chelsea

    📅 09 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 23 min read (4609 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

    ⏱️ ~23 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Xabi Alonso needed the cavalry – and referee Jarred Gillett – to stop Chelsea making a quick exit from the Carabao Cup and, boy, did they come up trumps for him.
    • Chelsea had looked to be heading out of the competition shortly after half-time, but, in Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers, Alonso has a cheat code that is capable of masking even the worst defending.
    • Industry observers note that alonso’s side have shared 26 goals in the five games they have played this season.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Xabi Alonso needed the cavalry – and referee Jarred Gillett – to stop Chelsea making a quick exit from the Carabao Cup and, boy, did they come up trumps for him.

    Chelsea had looked to be heading out of the competition shortly after half-time, but, in Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers, Alonso has a cheat code that is capable of masking even the worst defending.

    Industry observers note that alonso’s side have shared 26 goals in the five games they have played this season. It has certainly been an entertaining start by Chelsea’s latest manager.

    Recent findings suggest that palmer, Rogers and Pedro Neto stepped off the substitutes’ bench to complete a stunning rescue mission against Leeds United. Palmer scored twice, Neto once and Rogers helped himself to at least a hat-trick of assists. He claimed it was four, but the record books may say three.

    When it was unveiled Palmer had been awarded the player of the match, Rogers responded by saying: “Mate, I got four assists. I can’t believe that! That’s mental. He scored a pen!”.

    "Mate, I got four assists!" "That is criminal!" Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer arguing over the POTM award! 🤣 pic.twitter.com/X2PkPnSGDk.

    Chelsea had looked down and out, when, just three minutes after Alonso’s quadruple half-time change, Leeds doubled their lead. But four goals in an incredible 12-minute spell turned the tie on its head and it was Alonso’s substitutes who Chelsea had to thank.

    Palmer, with some help from Gillett, was the first to come to the home side’s rescue. Four minutes after Brenden Aaronson had put Leeds 2-0 up, Gillett pointed to the penalty spot after Daniel James had stood on the foot of Pep Chavarría.

    Sources indicate that it looked like a harsh decision on Leeds and proved to be almost as big of a game-changer as Alonso’s substitutions. Palmer stepped up to score the resulting penalty.

    Cole Palmer pulls one back for Chelsea from the spot! 🎯 pic.twitter.com/BUv6h1wTPQ.

    It has been revealed that “Nobody in the stadium, not one player was asking for a penalty and he gave the penalty,” Daniel Farke, the Leeds manager, noted. “All of a sudden their players came into the game. The momentum was on their side. Situations can change the whole momentum of the game.”.

    Stamford Bridge sensed a comeback and in the 55th minute, Rogers nudged the ball into the path of Palmer who produced a brilliant curling finish to beat Michael Zetterer, the Leeds goalkeeper.

    TWO goals in TWO minutes for Cole Palmer and Chelsea are level! 🥶 pic.twitter.com/sgDd3YUgA6.

    It has been revealed that reece James then went close, before Neto completed the turnaround on the hour mark. Palmer found Rogers, who in turn picked out Neto and he sent Stamford Bridge wild by sending his shot into the corner of the net.

    "This is a comeback of comebacks!" Pedro Neto scores and Chelsea have turned it around eleven minutes after going 2-0 down! 🤯 pic.twitter.com/FTPuWcFqEX.

    As Farke waited to make a quadruple substitution of his own, Danny Welbeck got in on the act by collecting the ball from Rogers, spinning and scoring.

    Class from Danny Welbeck 😤 pic.twitter.com/FUFKxlzXDz.

    That should have been that and the atmosphere could not have been more different from half-time, when Chelsea fans had booed off their side after watching them fall a goal behind.

    Reggie Watson, Chelsea’s 16-year-old debutant, Malo Gusto, Estêvão Willian and Jamie Gittens were hooked at half-time by Alonso, who noted: “For sure, I take responsibility for all of them. No player to blame. It’s the decisions that we took.

    Sources indicate that “I know that probably I haven’t taken the right decisions for them to show their best level. It’s something that I will analyse and learn from. So it’s my responsibility and we had to make decisions at half-time. And we have seen another second half with another quality.”.

    Industry observers note that goalkeeper Mike Penders was one of the nine changes made by Alonso. He produced a superb double-save to first keep out Aaronson and then recover to tip Tarik Muharemovic’s header out from the corner.

    Conor Coady was impressed with that Mike Penders double save in the first half 👏 pic.twitter.com/6NJqFDvnzk.

    According to recent reports, but the Belgian flapped at the corner, which gave Harry Wilson a second chance to get his delivery right. And he did just that by finding Muharemovic at the back post to head the ball into the net.

    Recent findings suggest that valentín Barco survived Alonso’s changes, but was partly at fault for Leeds’s second goal just after the break. He lost the ball and Ethan Ampadu galloped away from Rogers before crossing. Lukas Nmecha got the slightest of touches and Aaronsen smashed the ball into the net.

    "Chelsea cut apart AGAIN !" Brenden Aaronson makes it 2-0 to Leeds 🔥 pic.twitter.com/LlJNpqXHav.

    The substitutes then took over, as Chelsea shocked the visitors before Leeds substitute Dominic Calvert-Lewin gave his team hope by reducing the deficit with 15 minutes remaining.

    According to recent reports, any thoughts of a Leeds comeback were promptly erased, however, as Barco netted his first Chelsea goal from a Rogers pass, which may have taken a slight touch to deny him a fourth assist in the record books. Welbeck added a sixth in time added on.

    Industry observers note that valentín Barco gets Chelsea a FIFTH! 🫨 pic.twitter.com/XnhgvhBpL9.

    On the defeat by Chelsea, Farke stated: “The referee had the idea to give a penalty. No one in the stadium was asking for it, no one of their players was asking for it, but he spotted a situation where he thought he would give a penalty.

    “All of a sudden they scored the goal, then their players came into the game at half-time, the whole stadium after being relatively quiet for 60 minutes they of course were there then. The momentum was all of a sudden on their side. In football small situations can change the whole momentum of a game and this happened.”.

    It has been revealed that "100% I meant it!" 😅Morgan Rogers states he is really enjoying his football after he helped Chelsea beat Leeds 6-3 in the Carabao Cup! 🔵 pic.twitter.com/7uUQb6eIla.

    Industry observers note that here’s a reminder of the assist in question. Did Rogers mean it? Let us know in the comments beneath this live blog...

    It has been revealed that TWO goals in TWO minutes for Cole Palmer and Chelsea are level! 🥶 pic.twitter.com/sgDd3YUgA6.

    Industry observers note that "Mate, I got four assists!" "That is criminal!" Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer arguing over the POTM award! 🤣 pic.twitter.com/X2PkPnSGDk.

    On the message from the manager at half-time, Palmer told Sky Sports: “Just up the intensity, play a bit more, become more alive because I think the first half was flat, everyone agreed in the changing room, so we stepped up.

    Asked whether Alonso’s message was delivered calmly, he remarked: “At the start, but then he got a bit angry. But it was alright.”.

    On Chelsea’s half-time changes, Conor Coady mentioned on Sky Sports: “I think the credit goes down to [Alonso]. He made a bit of a statement by doing that at half-time. Four subs is a lot to do at half-time but it was needed. Listen, we said about the first half that it was kind of like the players hadn’t played with each other, and then the big guns came on... They were electric at times.”.

    A crazy match which was decided by Chelsea’s superb substitutes. Alonso took action at half-time and was rewarded with six goals in a madcap second half. Palmer hauled Chelsea back into the game, Rogers collected a handful of assists and Neto scored the go-ahead goal. You wonder what this match will do for the likes of Estevao and Gittens, though.

    Chelsea 6 Leeds United 3 (Welbeck) Pure reflexes from Welbeck, who diverts Barco’s wild effort beyond Zetterer.

    In a recent development, palmer has the hat-trick ball on his mind and attempts an audacious chip but just gets his angles wrong. Any guesses who laid on the chance? Rogers. Of course.

    Recent findings suggest that fans in the away end have resolved they have seen enough and are now heading towards the exits. Stach attempts to launch a counter but his raking cross-field ball is far too heavy.

    Rogers drifts out to the left and wins Chelsea a valuable corner. James walks over to take it to rapturous applause from supporters there.

    Leeds look to break but Wilson mistimes his run and is caught offside.

    There will be six minutes of time added on.

    Industry observers note that chance! Okafor darts inside of Neto and spins in a teasing ball to the back post but neither Calvert-Lewin nor Tanaka are able to reach it.

    Recent findings suggest that shouts for a Leeds penalty fail to pique the interest of referee Gillett. Gudmundsson was felled on the left of the box but the contact looked minimal.

    A tap on Barco’s head from Wilson provokes some histrionics from the Argentine but Jarred Gillett calms all parties down.

    Recent findings suggest that leeds are still pushing. Stach’s effort from eight yards out is closed down before Tanaka’s strike from the edge of the box is smothered by James.

    Alonso goes into the book, apparently for straying too far outside of his technical area.

    In a recent development, chelsea 5 Leeds United 3 (Barco) Rogers lays on his fourth assist of the match, driving towards the byline before flashing a searching ball across the face of goal which Barco spears past Zetterer at the far post. That should be that, right?

    Valentín Barco gets Chelsea a FIFTH! 🫨 pic.twitter.com/XnhgvhBpL9.

    We could be in for a blockbuster finish.

    Gudmundsson replaces debutant Bard down Leeds’ left.

    Chelsea 4 Leeds United 3 (Calvert-Lewin) Game back on? Okafor is afforded far too much space down the left by a tiring Chelsea back line and his cross finds Calvert-Lewin who plants the ball past Penders to reduce the deficit to just one goal. What a tie this has turned into!

    Leeds win a corner, which falls to Stach on the edge of the box but his effort is charged down.

    Recent findings suggest that it will be a source of acute anguish for Farke that Chelsea’s fourth goal came before he could make his four changes: Stach, Calvert-Lewin, Tanaka and Okafor eventually replace James, Nmecha, Longstaff and Aaronson. Conversely, it should be to Alonso’s credit that he took action early - his substitutes have decided this tie.

    Chelsea 4 Leeds United 2 (Welbeck) Rogers gallops on to a simple ball down the right channel and his cutback (towards Palmer) is picked up by Welbeck who spins before firing beyond Zetterer, leaving three Leeds defenders sprawled in front of him. He cares not, and absorbs the love of the crowd in the near corner.

    Class from Danny Welbeck 😤 pic.twitter.com/FUFKxlzXDz.

    Palmer goes close after having found a yard of space on the edge of the box. His strike spears through a thicket of limbs in Leeds’ box but Zetterer pulls off a strong save to deny the Englishman a quickfire hat-trick.

    Recent findings suggest that chelsea 3 Leeds United 2 (Neto) Just 11 minutes after going 2-0 down, Chelsea find themselves ahead. Palmer threads a through-ball through the middle for Rogers, who slides in front of his marker to an open Neto who sweeps the ball beyond Zetterer. Leeds punished for leaving themselves two vs two at the back there.

    It has been revealed that "This is a comeback of comebacks!" Pedro Neto scores and Chelsea have turned it around eleven minutes after going 2-0 down! 🤯 pic.twitter.com/FTPuWcFqEX.

    Chelsea have got their tails up and Palmer almost lays on a go-ahead goal but James cannot turn in his cross from the left.

    According to recent reports, chelsea 2 Leeds United 2 (Palmer) Wow! Palmer has turned this game on its head. And it’s so, so simple. Acheampong’s throw-in is knocked down by Rogers into the path of Palmer who works in from the right, passing the ball around a Leeds defender and past a rooted Zetterer.

    TWO goals in TWO minutes for Cole Palmer and Chelsea are level! 🥶 pic.twitter.com/sgDd3YUgA6.

    Chelsea 1 Leeds United 2 (Palmer) Palmer makes no mistake. He goes right, and while Zetterer guesses the right way he cannot get there and Chelsea are back in business.

    Recent findings suggest that cole Palmer pulls one back for Chelsea from the spot! 🎯 pic.twitter.com/BUv6h1wTPQ.

    It has been revealed that chavarria is caught by James in the box and the referee points to the spot. That came from nowhere.

    In a recent development, chelsea 0 Leeds United 2 (Aaronson) Amapadu deserves so much credit here. He steals the ball from Barco high, bursts beyond Rogers on the right and while Nmecha cannot turn in his cutback, Aaronson arrives late to stroke the ball past Penders and double Leeds’ lead.

    "Chelsea cut apart AGAIN !" Brenden Aaronson makes it 2-0 to Leeds 🔥 pic.twitter.com/LlJNpqXHav.

    Alonso resolves he has seen enough and rings the changes at the interval. Palmer, Rogers, James and Neto enter the fray in place of Estevao, Watson, Gittens and Gusto.

    Big cheers from the Chelsea fans at half-time, as Cole Palmer, Pedro Neto, Morgan Rogers and Reece James have all come on to warm up and are stripped off ready to play. Alonso is sending on the cavalry.

    The delayed kick-off has knocked us out of kilter with tonight’s Champions League matches, but here are the live scores:.

    Liverpool 2 Atletico Madrid 1Paris St-Germain 4 Slovan 0Napoli 0 Arsenal 0Sporting CP 1 Galatasaray 1.

    Boos at half-time from the Chelsea fans. Their team were pretty awful, but booing so early in the season. Really?

    Sources indicate that there is only one minute of time added on and Watson earns himself a booking for a late challenge on Wilson before the half-time whistle is blown. It will be interesting to see how long Alonso waits before turning to his bench.

    Justin, James and Wilson have got a lot of joy down Leeds’ right, rotating in Chavarria’s orbit. It has been difficult for Chelsea to pin them down and Gittens’ attacking threat has been blunted as he attempts to track their movements.

    Better from Chelsea. Watson does well to regain possession high and Estevao takes over, darting towards the by-line. His cutback is directed towards Welbeck but he is beaten to the ball by a Leeds toe and it is played behind for a corner which comes to nothing.

    Chelsea are really struggling to build up a head of steam, with individual mistakes proving costly.

    Gittens and Estevao both end up on the left and the former works infield before firing a shot at Zetterer which the German parries behind for a corner. Perhaps Chelsea’s most dangerous moment of the half.

    The corner is played short with the ball eventually falling to Barco on the edge of the box but his mis-hit effort trickles wide.

    Gittens rescues an overhit Acheampong cross and finds Barco on the edge of the box, but the Argentine’s effort is charged down. Leeds spring a counter and their sweeping move up field earns them a corner.

    Wilson floats another delivery to the back post to Muharemovic, but he cannot replicate his earlier goal.

    Recent findings suggest that farke will be delighted with what he has seen so far. It is all well and good Chelsea allowing Leeds the ball, but they have to break incisively when openings arise, and they have not done that.

    According to recent reports, major chance for Leeds! James bursts down the right and the Welsh winger dinks in a cross to the far post which Justin cannot get past Acheampong, but while Longstaff is first to the second ball, he can only sky the shot over the bar.

    It has been revealed that leeds’ goal has stirred something inside them and they look motivated to score a second. Ampadu debuts a long throw from the left which ricochets off a couple of players before rolling out for a Chelsea goal-kick.

    Sources indicate that chelsea 0 Leeds United 1 (Muharemovic) Set-pieces have been a massive feature of Leeds’ game this season and here they take the lead with the simplest of corner routines. Wilson floats the ball to the back post where Muharemovic is waiting, unmarked, and he loops a header over Penders into the net. Such a shame for the Chelsea keeper as he had just pulled off a stunning double-save.

    It has been revealed that "The set-piece routine does it again!" Tarik Muharemović puts Leeds in front against Chelsea! ⚡️ pic.twitter.com/UxeJ3xgL56.

    Barco slips on the far side and in doing so concedes a corner rather comically, to the delight of the travelling supporters. The delivery is met by Lacroix and Leeds are unable to create anything from the second phase of the set-piece.

    It has been revealed that there is an intriguing duel developing down Chelsea’s right as Bard looks to contain Estevao. The French wing-back has done a decent job so far.

    Estevao attempts to free himself of Bard’s clutches and drifts inside, Chavarria then almost picks him out with a cross from the left but Leeds just about clear their lines.

    Justin plays in a cultured through-ball from a wide-right position to James but Chavarria does well to snuff it out. Leeds are making the pitch as massive as possible and spaces are beginning to open up as they did at Fulham on the opening weekend.

    Although Penders’ shot-stopping has not yet been tested, he has shown some nifty footwork, sweeping up any loose balls that make it past Chelsea’s back three/five.

    It has been revealed that major chance! Chelsea spring a surprise attack as Chavarria sets Gittens away down the left. He works the ball infield to Welbeck who lays on a great chance for Estevao but Justin darts back to take the ball off the Brazilian’s toes. A brilliant piece of last-ditch defending.

    Gittens gets a shot away, a tame effort straight at Zetterer from 22 yards out as he cuts in from the left. The correct intent, though.

    Industry observers note that leeds look to circulate the ball across their back line. As mentioned pre-match, Chelsea will not mind letting their opponents get on the ball as they set out-of-possession traps. Aaronson eventually dribbles off the pitch on the far side.

    Chelsea’s Argentine midfielder, Valentin Barco, is being booed by the Leeds fans every time he touches the ball. Barco will already be used to getting that treatment, as it has even happened to him while he’s been a substitute this season.

    In other news, there’s a real Borussia Dortmund vibe to this Leeds away kit.

    Leeds supporters boo Argentina World Cup squad member Barco’s every touch, and another Leeds foul, this time Justin on Gittens, prompts a second Chelsea free-kick.

    In a recent development, A couple of early touches for Watson who plays a neat pass around the corner. Ampadu then lands a late tackle on Lacroix and Chelsea earn a free-kick in their own half.

    Although there are still some empty seats, we are finally under way. Chelsea in their customary all blue, kicking from right to left. Leeds in their yellow away strip.

    It has been revealed that chelsea and Leeds emerge from the tunnel, led out by Colwill and former Chelsea defender Ampadu. Here’s a reminder of the teams in full:.

    Chelsea Penders; Gusto, Acheampong, Lacroix, Colwill, Chavarria; Watson, Barco; Estevao, Gittens; Welbeck.

    Substitutes Martinez, Hato, Fofana, James, Neto, Palmer, Quenda, Rogers, Pedro.

    Leeds United Zetterer; Justin, Bijol, Muharemovic; James, Ampadu, Longstaff, Bard; Wilson, Aaronson; Nmecha.

    Substitutes Trafford, Gudmundsson, Elvedi, Bogle, Tanaka, Stach, Okafor, Calvert-Lewin, Bahoya.

    Daniel Farke believes Leeds can go far in the Carabao Cup this year 💪 pic.twitter.com/26ueAAUHoZ.

    Recent findings suggest that on the Brazilian winger’s opportunity tonight, Hasselbaink stated on Sky Sports: “He has to find his place. This is his opportunity... It’s not really an out-and-out left-wing [position] or a No 10 as he can play, but [with] good players it doesn’t matter where you put them on the pitch. He will find his spaces and he will be direct as he was when he came in against Arsenal. He is going to play for his place because he wants to play week-in, week-out.”.

    "He deserves to be there because of what he has shown" Xabi Alonso speaks about Reggie Watson with the 16-year-old set to make his Chelsea debut in their Carabao Cup game against Leeds 🌟 pic.twitter.com/AAn4Av3iEh.

    Tfl has closed South Kensington station after a “customer incident” meaning parts of the District Line have closed. The decision was then made to delay the match to give supporters more time to get to the stadium.

    Recent findings suggest that reggie Watson will become the fourth youngest player, aged 16, in Chelsea’s history. But he will have to wait a little bit longer for his debut as kick-off has been delayed by 15 minutes to 8.15pm.

    There will be a 15 minute delay to kick-off for our Carabao Cup third round tie with Leeds United tonight. The match will now begin at 20:15 BST. pic.twitter.com/MdDXpxgW09.

    A couple of cracking strikes from the Dutchman. Some player he was...

    "Good old days!" Jimmy Floyd Hasselbaink reflects on his goals for Leeds against Chelsea 🎞️ pic.twitter.com/bYjyFYIVIK.

    ChelseaAug 24: Fulham 2 Chelsea 3Aug 27: Chelsea 2 Luton Town 0 (Carabao Cup)Aug 30: Chelsea 4 Brighton 3Sep 6: Arsenal 2 Chelsea 1.

    LeedsAug 22: Nottingham Forest 0 Leeds 1Aug 25: Nottingham Forest 0 Leeds 2Aug 30: Leeds 1 Brentford 1Sep 5: Brighton 1 Leeds 1.

    As recently as March, a giant mural of Estêvão Willian appeared on the side of a building outside Stamford Bridge as the teenager threatened to become Chelsea’s number one poster boy.

    He may no longer hold top billing outside the club, following a summer in which Chelsea spent a club-record £117m on Morgan Rogers to complete a fearsome front three alongside Cole Palmer and João Pedro.

    A giant mural of the Brazilian teenager appeared on the side of a building close to Stamford Bridge in March.

    But inside Stamford Bridge, nothing has changed. Estêvão remains one of Chelsea’s star boys and is part of an “untouchable” group of players that also includes Palmer, Rogers and Pedro. Sources believe Estêvão is a player the club will look at rewarding with an improved contract in the coming months.

    Having already earned his Chelsea “untouchable” status, the next challenge for the 19-year-old winger – once nicknamed “Messinho” – is to make himself undroppable.

    Estêvão may not be a perfect fit for Xabi Alonso’s three-at-the-back formation that features two 10s – Palmer and Rogers – behind a striker. But the boy from Brazil is certainly not being squeezed out and Chelsea’s manager has spoken of the need to be flexible.

    Chelsea Penders; Gusto, Acheampong, Lacroix, Colwill, Chavarria; Watson, Barco; Estevao, Gittens; Welbeck.

    Substitutes Martinez, Hato, Fofana, James, Neto, Palmer, Quenda, Rogers, Pedro.

    Leeds United Zetterer; Justin, Bijol, Muharemovic; James, Ampadu, Longstaff, Bard; Wilson, Aaronson; Nmecha.

    Substitutes Trafford, Gudmundsson, Elvedi, Bogle, Tanaka, Stach, Okafor, Calvert-Lewin, Bahoya.

    Sources indicate that much has been made of Chelsea’s willingness to let the opposition have the ball under Xabi Alonso, but tonight they will likely be forced to dictate proceedings. In Leeds, they face one of only two sides who have completed fewer passes than them in the Premier League.

    Recent findings suggest that 1. Ian Hamilton in 1967: 16 years, four months and 15 days2. Kingsley Whiffen in 1967: 16 years, five months and six days3. Reggie Walsh in 2025: 16 years, six months and 11 days4. Reggie Watson in 2026: 16 years, seven months and 14 days5. Tommy Langley in 1974: 16 years, nine months and one day.

    Asked how he will approach the Carabao Cup this season, Daniel Farke said: “We’ll try to win it. That’s the quickest way to Europe and to some glory. Of course knowing that the Premier League will always have the priority and knowing that we are as successful as possible there, especially to reach our first goal to establish ourselves [at] this level.

    In a recent development, “We are not the favourites to win the Carabao Cup, we know this. Challenging, difficult games, but of course we travel to London in order to go through in the next round without doing anything stupid at this stage of the campaign because you also have to rotate a bit more and integrate a few newly introduced players. Nevertheless, we want to be at our best and anyhow possible we also want to go through to the next round.”.

    In a recent development, tonight represents an opportunity for 16-year-old Reggie Watson to announce himself at senior level. The central-midfielder caught Alonso’s eye during pre-season when the Spaniard mentioned of him: “Reggie Watson, a great midfielder. He thinks, he’s very collective, he’s very generous on the effort, intelligent with the ball”.

    “For his age, I’m really impressed with him.”.

    Dan James passes a late fitness test to make Daniel Farke’s starting XI.

    📋 Tonight's Starting XI pic.twitter.com/MQKQtGZm8c.

    Industry observers note that reggie Watson, 16, son of former Wigan midfielder Ben (of 2013 FA Cup final fame), makes his full Chelsea debut and becomes the club’s fourth youngest player. Estevao, Jamie Gittens and Danny Welbeck replace Alonso’s thrilling forward three, who are on the bench.

    Chelsea XI Penders; Gusto, Acheampong, Lacroix, Colwill, Chavarria; Watson, Barco; Estevao, Gittens; Welbeck.

    Industry observers note that your Blues to face Leeds United in the #CarabaoCup! #CFC pic.twitter.com/636SOiUXVB.

    Industry observers note that good evening and welcome to live coverage of tonight’s Carabao Cup third-round tie between Chelsea and Leeds United. This is a rematch of last season’s FA Cup semi-final which Chelsea edged by a single Enzo Fernández goal, but plenty has changed since then. Xabi Alonso has taken over the reins at Stamford Bridge and made a promising start, reeling off three wins before losing to Arsenal in an absorbing contest last Sunday. Chelsea are not involved in European competition this season, so the domestic cups represent an avenue to silverware, as well as an opportunity to tinker.

    Industry observers note that in Alonso’s way, though, stands a Leeds team whose manager, Daniel Farke, told the media on Tuesday that his side are aiming to win the Carabao Cup. Farke has overseen an impressive run of form, having lost only two of their previous 16 competitive matches in a stretch that extends back to March. Two wins at Nottingham Forest preceded draws against Brentford and Brighton to keep Leeds undefeated this term. Farke has suggested he will rotate in west London to “integrate upcoming players” having brought in seven new recruits during the summer.

    If Leeds are to reach the next round, they must reverse a heavily one-sided head-to-head record against their hosts, who have won each of their past 10 cup meetings (three in the League Cup, seven in the FA Cup). In fact, Chelsea have lost at this stage of the competition just once in the past 15 years, and that was against Pep Guardiola’s Manchester City four seasons ago.

    Alonso broke up the exhilarating “JP Morgan” band (João Pedro, Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers) for Chelsea’s victory over Luton Town in the previous round, handing starts to Danny Welbeck and Estêvão. Players such as Jamie Gittens and Geovany Quenda are also waiting in the wings and may get chances to impress tonight. Mike Penders could also be in line for a start between the sticks.

    💡 Key Takeaways
