    The Timing Game – MH

    📅 31 Mar 2025 | ⏱️ 21 min read (4142 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Spielverlagerung

    ⏱️ ~21 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • von Next Generation am 31.03.2025 in den Kategorien Tactical Theory mit 1 Kommentar.
    • Industry observers note that the Timing Game describes a playing philosophy in which the right moment of an action is crucial.
    • “Brighton is a master of passing the ball to the free man but recognising when to pass the ball to the free man and moving at the right time.” – Pep Guardiola.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    von Next Generation am 31.03.2025 in den Kategorien Tactical Theory mit 1 Kommentar.

    Industry observers note that the Timing Game describes a playing philosophy in which the right moment of an action is crucial. It not only allows pressing traps to be reversed but also enables teams to break down deep defensive blocks with precision. In the Premier League, Brighton’s then-manager Roberto De Zerbi took this tactical approach to a new level.

    “Brighton is a master of passing the ball to the free man but recognising when to pass the ball to the free man and moving at the right time.” – Pep Guardiola.

    According to recent reports, the core idea of the Timing Game is to react to the opponent’s movement at precisely the right moment. Pressing traps can be reversed by first triggering and manipulating the opponent’s press and then bypassing it through changes in speed and direction. Since opposition pressing actions are highly dynamic, this approach is particularly effective against high-pressing teams. Consequently, the Timing Game allows teams to dominate pressing situations in their own buildup play. Additionally, because opponent movements can be triggered independently of the game phase, the Timing Game can also be applied against deep defensive blocks.

    Regarding the role of timing in De Zerbi’s buildup play, René Maric (RM) explained in a 2023 interview with SkySports:.

    „The biggest thing in the build-up is the control of rhythm. If you look at Guardiola, he does it with the speed of the passes and then they carry the ball when they don’t have pressure. De Zerbi does it more with the moment of the pass, the lure, the sole on the ball, opening space with the pass rather than the carry. How you control the rhythm and progress through space will be big in the future. That development has already started.“.

    Industry observers note that this article examines the dimensions and functioning of the Timing Game. Additionally, it analyzes the impact of a team’s own positioning, as well as the manipulation, anticipation, and triggering of the opponent’s press (or movements). The following sections will then explore the action of bypassing the opponent, the potential issues that arise within the Timing Game, and possible solutions to these challenges.

    This section is an attempt to highlight the various facets of the Timing Game and football in general. Different playing philosophies prioritize different dimensions. In the Timing Game described here, particular focus is placed on the timing of dynamics in relation to the opponent.

    To gain a better understanding of the principles of the Timing Game, the following section presents and explains its different dimensions. This makes it clear how the Timing Game differs from the focus of positional play and relationism but can also be combined with them. Although the game dimensions are less key for the practical implementation of the Timing Game, they can be useful for further developing this concept or other coaching philosophies.

    Recent findings suggest that the most notable dimension of the Timing Game is the temporal dimension. The crucial factors are the speed and timing of decision-making. The timing of a progressive action should generally coincide with the opponent’s movement. The primary focus is therefore on the exact moment of an action.

    A second important dimension is that of dynamics. The dynamic dimension of the Timing Game revolves around explosiveness and changes in rhythm. Changes in dynamics can be decisive both in relation to one’s own play and in terms of directional shifts in relation to the opponent. Ultimately, the goal is to create the strongest possible reciprocal acceleration in the opponent.

    Recent findings suggest that in the dimension of individual performance factors, the focus is on footballing competencies such as technical and athletic abilities. In the Timing Game, ball control is a crucial factor, as it significantly affects a player’s pressing resistance. Ball control involves both the ability to recognize a situation and the technical capability to handle the ball under pressure at any time. This skill is particularly notable in the Timing Game, as it provides an advantage during the opponent’s pressing phase.

    In a recent development, the causal-relational dimension deals with the cause-and-effect principle in interactions between teammates and opponents. There is a causal relationship both between the opponent’s defensive approach and the method of bypassing them, as well as between a teammate’s action and the resulting ball action. The following examples illustrate this:.

    In relationism, interactions between teammates are particularly emphasized to enable optimal interplay. Due to the complexity of this dimension, I have linked MR’s seminar “The Future of the Game” here.

    In the spatial dimension, the focus is on controlling specific zones of the pitch. This is particularly crucial in positional play, where the aim is to control the game through ball possession and spatial occupation. In the Timing Game, however, the goal is to reach the space behind the opponent. Since this space is constantly changing, it cannot strictly be defined as a fixed pitch zone. However, the spatial dimension does play a role in the preparatory positioning of the Timing Game. This article contains a dedicated section on the optimal positioning in preparation for the Timing Game.

    In the Timing Game, the moment of an action is primarily decisive. The moment of action is always triggered by the opponent’s movement. The more intense the opponent’s movement, the easier it is to bypass them. This is because, once the Timing Game is triggered, the opponent should be bypassed as diagonally opposed to their movement as possible. This forces the opponent into a maximal change of direction and dynamics.

    The pressing near one’s own penalty area is bypassed diagonally opposite to the direction of the press.

    Industry observers note that A temporal advantage is created over the opponent, who initially has to accelerate in the opposite direction and loses time. The space that opens up behind the advancing opponent can be played most effectively. Representing the functioning of the Timing Game, the principle of “Lure and Shock” could be used. The opponent is first “lured” into the movement and then “shocked” by being bypassed.

    The Timing Game is particularly effective during the opponent’s transition from a deeper to a higher pressing setup. At the moment of transition between ordered pressing phases, the opponent’s structure is often lacking, as the distances between the players change. Additionally, movement is present on all positions of the opponent, which can be exploited for the Timing Game. The direction of the opponent’s movement is also crucial, as during the transition from a deeper to a higher pressing phase, vertical movement away from the goal dominates, allowing spaces towards the opponent’s goal to be exploited.

    This specific moment of the opponent’s pressing transition into a higher setup cannot be found in the classic phase model of the game according to Van Gaal. Depending on the perspective, it would be classified as part of either the team’s own possession phase or the opponent’s possession phase, even though it is significantly more complex and interesting than other possession situations. The opponent is essentially in a type of defensive transition into attack from the opponent’s ball possession, while the own team takes advantage of this moment and transitions from their own ball possession into a kind of offensive transition.

    The Timing Game, however, does not only work during transitions between different pressing setups, but also independently of the game phase, and thus also within the framework of the opponent’s attacking press. The opponent’s movement in attacking pressing usually does not need to be triggered additionally. Instead, it is more about anticipating the moment when the opponent’s attacking press is triggered. At the moment of pressing initiation, there is a very high dynamic on multiple positions of the opponent in (diagonal) vertical directions, which allows the pressing to be bypassed with suitable movements at the moment of initiation. Particularly, the opponent’s pressing traps can be bypassed at the moment of initiation through a corresponding pre-rehearsed anticipation and movement.

    According to recent reports, depending on the individual pressing patterns of the opponent, preparations should be made for the timing and manner of bypassing. For example, man-marking in attacking pressing can be bypassed differently than ball-oriented or hybrid marking schemes. Particularly against man-marking, it is crucial in the Timing Game to initially provoke dynamics in the opponent through various runs, in order to then bypass them in the opposite direction. If dynamics are not created through own runs, there is often little movement from the opponent in the second and third layers that could be exploited.

    Because dynamics are also created in the opponent’s man-marking in the second and third layers, multiple layers can be bypassed.

    The pressing triggers and pressing traps also differ depending on the type of attacking press, so anticipating the moments of the Timing Game requires prior analysis of the opponent. A very commonly used pressing trigger is a backward pass to the goalkeeper from a higher defensive line. A common reaction is for the goalkeeper to play the ball long under pressure, usually resulting in a loss of possession. In the Timing Game, a team would create passing options behind the opponent through collective movements at the moment the opponent triggers their press. Specific movements and methods for bypassing the press will be discussed in more detail later in the article.

    Individual pressing patterns also include the opponent’s pressing structure itself. Here too, individual weaknesses can be diagnosed and exploited in advance. When the opponent presses from a 4-4-2, they often have an under-populated central area. Of course, this cannot be generalized, as, for example, the ball-far midfielder or an aggressive center-back may situationally reinforce the center. However, if this is not the case, an inverse run by the full-back at the moment the press is triggered could be useful to play into the space behind the press against the dynamics. It can be stated that the Timing Game, against different opponents with different individual pressing patterns, influences the movements made to bypass the press.

    The Timing Game can also work against deep-lying opponents. However, it is more difficult here because, in general, there is less movement away from the goal, and the opponent attacks in a more passive manner. The deep-lying opponent’s goal is to close the space near the goal. It will be crucial to trigger the opponent’s movement or pressing and lure the opponent out. We will go into more detail on such trigger actions later.

    In a recent development, in summary, the following rules for the Timing Game depending on the opponent’s pressing can be established: The deeper the opponent is positioned, the less dynamic movement there is away from their own goal. Therefore, the time window for bypassing the press is shorter. The more passive the opponent acts, the less frequently there is opponent movement. As a result, there will be fewer opportunities to bypass the press. Nevertheless, the Timing Game can be used independently of the game phase through trigger actions.

    According to recent reports, the team’s formation in possession should be adapted to the challenges of the Timing Game. It should create central connections through a vertical/diagonal alignment. This way, more layers can be incorporated into the dynamics, and more passing options can be created. More passing windows open up at the moment of triggering through a variety of passing angles. In the event of a loss of possession, it also allows for more effective counter-pressing.

    Additionally, it can be useful to work with asymmetries and overloads. Overloading the own buildup zone is particularly effective when the opponent closes down and applies high pressure. This lures the opponent and allows them to be bypassed with a few passes. In the linked video example, De Zerbi’s Shakhtar Donetsk uses a strategy of having 7 players in their own penalty area during a goal kick to lure the opponent out.

    Nothing to see here, just a completely normal build-up pic.twitter.com/vOcvRPVKdf.

    — Jamie Hamilton (@stirling_j) April 28, 2022.

    According to recent reports, problems in the Timing Game arise when there is an overload in the own buildup zone if the opponent does not press. The progression in the game is lacking because offensive passing options are not available. Also problematic is the static overload of the last line. If players remain in their specific spaces in the last line, passing options necessary to bypass the opponent’s press are missing.

    Recent findings suggest that another way to structure the team to prepare for the Timing Game is by leaving a specific area vacant. If the opponent attempts to press, this space is usually left unoccupied by the opponent as well. Subsequently, the space can be attacked and played into from the second line in the opposite direction. If the space is still occupied, the numerical advantage in a ball-near area can be exploited. Real Madrid often employs such structures or space-drawing runs in preparation for their actual attacking play with the ball.

    Industry observers note that in the Timing Game, the moment the opponent begins to press must be anticipated as early as possible. Possible indicators for early recognition of a pressing moment include: the opponent’s approach towards the ball-carrying teammate, the shrinking of distances between the ball-near opponents and their teammates, and the forward dynamics of the opponent. A defensive line with equal numbers or an advancing defender is also an early recognition feature. Lastly, specific pressing triggers should be identified through video analysis in advance.

    An exemplary player for effective pressing resistance is Sergio Busquets, who, with his excellent ball control, was regularly able to anticipate and resolve pressing situations. In this 2017 article, TR and MR wrote about Busquets’ qualities.

    Industry observers note that what is particularly interesting is triggering the opponent’s attacking press. There are a variety of very interesting trigger actions. One variation used by De Zerbi is the use of the sole on the ball to wait. This plays on the impatience of the opponent. The following quote and video clearly demonstrate the effectiveness of this trigger action.

    “It’s so fascinating to watch (…) when the ball goes to the center back, they freeze the game. (…) As soon as the pressing action happened, they then had this meticulously designed mechanism of up-back-throughs and third man connections (…).” – Jamie Hamilton, 3rd Circle Podcast.

    — Jamie Hamilton (@stirling_j) January 13, 2025.

    It has been revealed that another option is a pass triggered by speed. This pass should be played as slowly as possible and as rapidly as necessary. The slow pass provokes the opponent’s pressing. At the same time, by the receiver moving towards the ball, the dynamics can immediately be reversed. This facilitates the transition into the action of bypassing or dribbling past the opponent. The pass direction should ideally be diagonal toward one’s own goal. This maximizes the reversal of dynamics.

    According to recent reports, another approach is to play into the pressure, only to then “bounce” back into the direction of the opponent’s pressing path. The opponent is initially led to believe they have access by playing into the pressure. By bouncing the ball into the pressing direction, the opponent is forced to continue their run.

    Sources indicate that the classic way of forcing a passive opponent into movement is dribbling. The opponent is eventually made to press. However, it is also much harder to generate a dynamic shift and surprise effect, as the dribbling is already in the direction of play. Therefore, it is helpful if dribbling-skilled players attack the opponent in order to maintain the unpredictability of the next action with quick changes of direction. Alternatively, passes that bypass the opponent after dribbling in the opposite direction of the dribble path can create a dynamic shift in the opponent.

    Against deep-lying opponents, the inside diagonal is a good method to force defenders on the last line to step out a few meters. When the ball is played diagonally from the outside to the center, the central defender steps out a few steps. This can be exploited in the opposite direction. The effect is enhanced by a player letting the ball pass, as immediately after, the defender’s back can be attacked. This move is known in relationism as Escadinha.

    — Svids (@Svids8) February 23, 2025.

    In a recent development, after the pressing trigger, the opponent should be bypassed through dynamic, diagonal directional changes. The direction of the first action should ideally not move away from the pressure but rather target, go over, or through it to attack the opponent’s movement. Instead of directly passing to the free player (e.g., the goalkeeper), a progressive, diagonal ball should be chosen.

    Sources indicate that to create passing options in the desired direction, specific movements are crucial. There are also various fundamental principles for this. The start of the ball action should be as late as possible but as early as necessary.

    The timing of the movement of teammates should coincide with the moment the press begins, so they can be available to receive the ball under pressure, but not too early to avoid being caught by the opponent’s dynamic.

    Dynamic movement should also be generated in the second and third layers to have the opportunity to bypass multiple layers. Otherwise, there is a risk of opponents from the second layer, who create covering shadows, not being affected by the opposing dynamic. In a less compact space behind the first pressing line, the dynamics can occur in stages, so the layers are played one after the other.

    It is notable that after an action, the next layer should be attacked immediately to maintain the dynamic.

    In a recent development, the decisive action to overcome the opponent can be individual, group, or team tactical in nature. Below are specific examples of such actions.

    Industry observers note that A feint in the moment of pressing initiation can lead to bypassing the opponent. In the linked video, Musiala’s movement at the right moment leads to the goal. Although this movement is likely executed intuitively by Musiala at the right time, it can certainly be tactically repeated. The feint falls into the above-described phase of the pressing transition from a deeper to a higher pressing line, which is why Denmark’s player spacing is incorrect and the deep coverage is absent.

    Brilliant angle of Jamal Musiala’s goal from last night. 🇩🇪#Germany #Denmark #Euro #Analysis pic.twitter.com/xl2MDgvXwb.

    — Jamie Kyte (@jamielkyte) June 30, 2024.

    Individually tactical, the first touch can be used both as a triggering action and as an overcoming action. By skillfully triggering the opponent’s movement, it may be enough to simply play the ball past the opponent or through their legs. The first touch is made as far as possible but as close as necessary to allow the player to regain possession of the ball immediately in front of the opponent. This is clearly seen at the very beginning of Woltemade’s first goal in the following video.

    ⚽#woltemade #u21 pic.twitter.com/mpdKiB4inJ.

    — ran (@ransport) March 25, 2025.

    The no-look pass can also be a variant to surprise the opponent against the dynamics and running direction.

    Madrid pic.twitter.com/z2nyPVIuPi.

    — Svids (@Svids8) December 19, 2024.

    In a recent development, florian Wirtz’s dribbles may initially seem unremarkable. However, upon closer observation, it becomes clear that Wirtz uses slight delays instead of flashy tricks to trigger the opponent’s movement, and then he moves the ball past the defender. This is also a form of timing play at the individual tactical level.

    @MunichComps pic.twitter.com/qNsq4Ljltc.

    — thomassist (@thomassist25_) January 27, 2025.

    On the group tactical level, up-back-through (steil-klatsch) combinations are ideal for breaking into depth at the right moment. Here, the previously described positioning in preparation for the timing play is crucial. As many levels as possible should be occupied to open passing angles and options. The lay-off play has the advantage of being able to overcome the opponent with simple passes. It is remarkable how each of these passes is played against the opponent’s pressing direction, preventing the opponent from getting access to the ball.

    — ファンキーヤング (@funkyyoung) November 19, 2024.

    Different variations of the play through the third man are also very effective. In the following video, the effectiveness can be admired at minute 0:13, using the example of the left center-back starting in the wrong direction.

    — Svids (@Svids8) February 20, 2025.

    Other possibilities in the group tactical area include one-twos against the dynamics, space-creating runs, counter movements, or dynamic zone rotations.

    There are also team tactical variations for overcoming the opponent in the timing game. One such variation is playing the second ball directly into the backline with an appropriate zone overload at the moment the pressing is triggered. The preparatory positioning is the team tactical element here.

    A team tactical counter movement could also be considered, where all players in the forward zones drop back, increasing the pressing distance to create more dynamic movement. At the same time, a player from the second line attacks deeply in the opposite direction.

    In a recent development, one problem with the timing play is overcoming the covering shadow of the first pressing opponent. As the approaching opponent generates an increasingly larger covering shadow in a well-prepared pressing situation, passing options become limited. This can be solved through an individual tactical overcoming action, such as a dribble, a first touch, or others. Additionally, certain combination plays can help overcome the first pressing player. A back-up-back-through combination could be effective, where the first pass is played over a short distance to a nearby teammate (back), followed by an up-back-through combination to open latest passing angles.

    The short back pass to the goalkeeper, who has moved up into the defensive line, can bypass the covering shadow of the first pressing player.

    Industry observers note that another problem could arise against teams with a very high pressing intensity. Since it is necessary to play into the pressure and trigger the pressing, one is systematically exposed to this high intensity repeatedly. However, this can also be used to one’s advantage. Opponents with high intensity also have high dynamics, which can be played against with greater effectiveness. Additionally, there is usually a high number of opponents in the attacking zones. Therefore, it is advisable to attack the farthest free space as directly as possible.

    Recent findings suggest that hybrid pressing can also cause problems in the timings game. Since individual players act in specific spaces, responding situationally to regain possession of the ball, they do not necessarily carry the dynamics of the pressing players. As a result, they are more difficult to play past. However, certain off-ball runs could provide solutions here. One example would be the outside defender making a diagonal run into space far from the ball.

    In a recent development, lastly, there are concerns when pressing the opponent during goal kicks. All playing philosophies face problems here, as the conditions to break out of the situation are not ideal. The ball is not in motion, the opponent can organize, and the playing field is limited by the goal line behind. Additionally, the risk is higher due to the proximity to the goal. The timings game would generate dynamics in the opponent by various runs from teammates, in order to reach the opponent’s back at the right moment.

    The concept of dynamically timing a play to exploit the opponent’s movement at the right moment is already seen in practice. However, with a more deliberate approach, it can become more accessible to a wider range of players and even more effective. It holds the potential to bypass pressing traps and break down deep-lying defenses. It is not only applicable throughout the field but can also be effective with different numbers of players.

    In a recent development, the dynamic timing play concept developed here is heavily focused on the reference point of the “opponent.” Another possible concept of timing could place more emphasis on the teammate, focusing on relational interactions between players. This concept would be more closely aligned with the relationalism theory. Using the dimensions outlined here, different game concepts can be created and further developed.

    The timing play should be used as a complementary element to complete one’s overall playing philosophy. It provides a different perspective on tactical analysis than what would be possible with static graphics, such as those on a tactic board. Therefore, it should expand an analyst’s perspective on this complex game by adding an additional dimension.

For MH, football is not just a game, it’s a way of life. He can be found on X under Mh_sv5 and LinkedIn.

    Victor Wembanyama has dunked so much he hurt his hand, so he came up with a unique solution: The 'shunk'

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (535 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Remember at the end of Space Jam, when Michael Jordan launched himself off of the butt of a MonStar to dunk from the half-court line?
    • Industry observers note that let's set the stage here.
    • In a recent development, did Wemby just...
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Remember at the end of Space Jam, when Michael Jordan launched himself off of the butt of a MonStar to dunk from the half-court line? Well, imagine the exact opposite of that play. Instead of an impossibly long dunk, Thursday night's NBA action gave us an impossibly short jumper.

    Industry observers note that let's set the stage here. The San Antonio Spurs are leading the Los Angeles Clippers by 12 points with under four minutes remaining. Victor Wembanyama is alone under the basket. He led the NBA with 71 dunks on the season to that point. Nobody else, as of the beginning of play Thursday, had reached even 50. But Wembanyama does not take this opportunity to slam down dunk No. 72, at least not intentionally. No, San Antonio's Martian with an eight-foot wingspan jumps directly in front of the basket... and flicks his wrist downward in what was seemingly a shooting motion. It swishes through the rim. Two points.

    In a recent development, did Wemby just... shoot it from above the rim??? 🤯😲 pic.twitter.com/1YDxy8mwy8.

    Industry observers note that officially, it will count as dunk No. 72 on the season for Wembanyama. Unofficially, as coined by Spurs broadcaster Sean Elliott, it was the first "shunk" of his season. Or, well, perhaps anyone's. It takes a perfect storm of circumstances to create a shunk: an uncommonly large basketball player, a lane open enough to ensure no defensive resistance, and perhaps rarest of all, a center disinterested in dunking.

    In a recent development, that begs an important question: what compelled this maneuver? Well, as is so often the case, necessity was the mother of invention.

    Wembanyama has a blister on his right hand. He doesn't know when exactly it came, but he knows where it came from. "It definitely came from dunking a lot," he told reporters after the game Thursday. The math here checks out. Wembanyama dunked 178 times in 64 games last season. That's around 2.8 dunks per game. Even if we discount the shunk, he's at 71 dunks through 16 games this season, or around 4.4.

    Industry observers note that fortunately for the Spurs, Wembanyama has no looks to stop dunking, "but if I can avoid it, I would," he noted after the win. The blister, according to Wembanyama, is quite painful. You'd hardly know it from watching him play. Wembanyama is averaging career-highs in points, rebounds, blocks and field goal percentage thus far this season. He is leading a 13-3 Spurs team that is tied for the NBA's best record thus far, and along with Luka Dončić, he is one of the two heavy favorites to win this season's MVP award.

    If he's looking for a fringe benefit here, the "shunk" might save him from the "run and just dunk" esque criticism that Giannis Antetokounmpo recevied during his MVP pursuits. This is genuine innovation in the short-distance conversion space. Innovation is rarely in short supply in San Antonio. Earlier this week, Wembanyama threw himself multiple passes off of the backboard in a single quarter. Every time you turn on a Spurs game, there's a real chance Wembanyama does something you've never seen before, and the shunk is no exception.

    Inside Diego Gomez's remarkable rise to Premier League's king of the wondergoal: Plucked from a rural Paraguayan village at 13, doing Lionel Messi's running for him at Inter Miami and starring as Brighton's aggressive machine

    📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1452 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

    ⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Published: 02:00 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 08:07 EST, 21 November 2026.
    • Scattered across the flatlands of Paraguay’s deeply religious Misiones District, where families rely on the land to feed themselves through cattle ranching and cotton production, the people are idolising one of their own.
    • Recent findings suggest that diego Gomez’s ascent from the humble beginnings of a farmer’s son to the heart of a Premier League title race is a Hollywood director’s dream.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By TARA ANSON-WALSH, FOOTBALL REPORTER.

    Published: 02:00 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 08:07 EST, 21 November 2026.

    Scattered across the flatlands of Paraguay’s deeply religious Misiones District, where families rely on the land to feed themselves through cattle ranching and cotton production, the people are idolising one of their own.

    Recent findings suggest that diego Gomez’s ascent from the humble beginnings of a farmer’s son to the heart of a Premier League title race is a Hollywood director’s dream. While it is a script that has been read many times before, like an old movie or a classic song, it is also one that never gets old.

    In this particular iteration, it begins on the dirt tracks of Mburika Reta, which literally translates to the ‘land of donkeys’ in Paraguay’s native Guarani, before winding through the country's capital, Asuncion, and briefly stopping among the palm-lined suburbs of Miami alongside Sergio Busquets and Lionel Messi. It is now gathering pace on England’s south coast, where Brighton find themselves in the unfamiliar territory of hunting down the Premier League champions.

    Gomez is the epitome of Fabian Hurzeler’s machine: energetic, aggressive and relentlessly forward-thinking. It is through this collective sense of selflessness that the Seagulls are second in the table, having already defeated both league leaders Arsenal and Manchester City this season. And for Hurzeler’s versatile midfielder, every performance and goal is a reminder of the moments that forged him.

    ‘He always told me to play forward and, when I have the ball, to have no fear,’ the 23-year-old stated last year of his former team-mate Messi.

    Cue a spectacular goal from the halfway line against Crystal Palace last month, the Amex crowd growing feverish as the ball sailed over Walter Benitez before crashing into the back of the net.

    Diego Gomez pictured as a young teen playing for Libertad (left), is now thriving for Paraguay (right) and one of Brighton's most important players.

    Gomez is congratulated by Pascal Gross after scoring a brilliant goal against Brentford.

    Another rapidly followed against Brentford last weekend, with Gomez barely bringing the ball under control before hooking it into the net from 25 yards out with his supposedly weaker left foot, leaving half of his team-mates clutching their heads in disbelief.

    Inevitably Gomez’s rise has not been without its setbacks. It was his mistimed tackle on Desire Doue, stretching out a leg to topple the French winger in the penalty area, that led to the heartache of Paraguay’s World Cup elimination this summer, after Kylian Mbappe slotted home the resulting spot-kick.

    Yet rather than be defined by this mistake, Gomez returned home to a hero’s welcome, mobbed by locals as he was paraded through the streets of the usually sleepy San Juan Bautista in an open-top car.

    Industry observers note that ‘He has the right attitude towards football,’ Hurzeler noted shortly after his arrival. ‘He loves to play. You can feel his passion in every talk with him.’.

    Across his 10 appearances this season, Gomez has won 66 duels, more than any Brighton player. His 35 aerial duels won, second behind only Croatian centre back Luka Vuskovic, point to his impressive spring, and he has won 10 tackles, again more than any other Brighton player.

    At the other end of the pitch, meanwhile, he has taken the most touches in the opposition box and has scored two goals and recorded two assists this season.

    While Gomez’s physique gives the impression of a battering ram, he is surprisingly speedy, recording Brighton’s fastest top speed of the season against Chelsea at 21.01mph.

    But who is this kid who was plucked out of nowhere? Who, at the age of 13, moved four hours away from his rural village to the capital to play football, navigating the bus networks as a child to get to training at FC Libertad before a move to join David Beckham’s glitzy side arrived seven years later?

    Gomez, seen with his partner Geraldine Villagra, has taken an unusual route to the top.

    In this case, it was Inter Miami who did the plucking, with Gomez identified by Brighton’s scouting network while he was playing in the MLS in 2024. Gomez formally joined the club as a 21-year-old in a deal worth £11million in January 2025, having agreed the move six months earlier.

    Sources indicate that former Brighton centre back Gordon Greer is now the club’s pathway development manager and spoke regularly to Gomez during this time, travelling to Florida to see him during the latter stages of the MLS season. It’s fair to say he liked what he found.

    It has been revealed that ‘We knew that he would do well because of his application,’ Greer states. ‘He was just a really talented, young, hungry footballer. You could see that he had raw potential, and I think Brighton do that really well. They sign players who have got room to improve.

    It has been revealed that ‘The one thing about Diego that is really impressive is his attitude, his work rate. He’s a really driven character and he’s such a humble kid. You can ask Diego to do certain things and he’ll give it his all, no matter what you ask him to do, whether he’s good at it or not. As a coach, it must be amazing to have someone like that in your team.’.

    In a recent development, during his six-month wait for the move, Gomez undertook regular English lessons, tuned in to Brighton’s games on television and spoke to Hurzeler about the areas he could improve before making the switch. All of that left him with a couple of weeks’ head start, which in Premier League terms is massive.

    Meanwhile, Brighton’s plethora of South American footballers at the time, most notably Julio Enciso, who played alongside him at Libertad, helped him settle quickly. So too did Gomez’s girlfriend, Geraldine Villagra, who moved to Brighton to live with him, while his family regularly visit from Paraguay.

    Gomez is the epitome of Fabian Hurzeler’s energetic machine for the Seagulls.

    Industry observers note that spending 18 months alongside Messi, Busquets and Luis Suarez was also another crucial step in Gomez’s development, despite his understandable initial nerves. He forged a strong understanding with Messi on the pitch and was the engine that enabled the Argentine genius to thrive. Much like at Brighton, though, that did not stop Gomez from producing moments of magic of his own.

    In a recent development, ‘The fact that he had these superstars in the team probably helped him,’ Greer claims. ‘We don’t have any superstars in our team like Messi, but everyone gives their all.

    ‘At Inter Miami, Messi was by far the best player, but Diego did a lot of the running for him and had a fantastic season in which he contributed a number of goals and assists. He just worked away at it. Regardless of the kind of environment you put him in, he finds a way through it.’.

    The audacity of Gomez’s two recent goals, the strike against Palace that inevitably won the Premier League Goal of the Month award for October and the Brentford one which is firmly in contention for November, almost contradicts that industrious nature. Has Greer been surprised by them?

    It has been revealed that ‘He scored some really good goals for Inter Miami, but not as good as the ones he’s scored of late for us,’ he indicates. ‘He wants to achieve massive things. It’s no surprise... well, it is a surprise when you see him stick one in the top corner with his left foot!’.

    Gomez endeared himself to many when he broke down during a pre-World Cup press conference while speaking about the privilege of representing his country, and he remains deeply aware of where he has come from.

    Earlier this year, Brighton chose to extend their UNICEF partnership to Paraguay, with Gomez becoming an ambassador for a programme that aims to develop young people's skills and confidence through sport and will reach thousands of children across the nation, a role he regards as a great honour.

    After Paraguay’s elimination from the World Cup, Gomez attended one of the events in Asuncion, where he first plied his trade and where UNICEF will soon roll out the programme.

    ‘During his personal time, after coming back from the World Cup, he could have done lots of other things and chose instead to do that,’ Anna Easthope, Brighton’s head of marketing, adds. ‘He realises the impact of meeting kids, giving them inspiration and letting them know that sport is for everyone.’.

    If a hero’s welcome followed World Cup elimination, imagine the reception a Premier League title would bring to Misiones.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The offseason's biggest domino fell late Sunday evening: Tarik Skubal agreed to a nine-year, $450 million contract with the Mets.
    • It should be a busy week on the hot stove leading up to the expiration of the collective bargaining agreement at 11:59 p.m.
    • According to recent reports, the Yankees and left-hander Brent Suter have agreed to a one-year contract worth $4 million, reports the Latest York Post.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The offseason's biggest domino fell late Sunday evening: Tarik Skubal agreed to a nine-year, $450 million contract with the Mets. It is far and away the richest pitching contract in history, crushing Yoshinobu Yamamoto's $325 million deal with the Dodgers. The Mets still have other things to address, including adding another starter, but they landed the winter's best free agent.

    It should be a busy week on the hot stove leading up to the expiration of the collective bargaining agreement at 11:59 p.m. ET on Dec. 1. Here are our top 50 free agents and top 25 trade candidates, and the vital offseason dates and deadlines you need to know. Here now are Monday's hot stove happenings.

    According to recent reports, the Yankees and left-hander Brent Suter have agreed to a one-year contract worth $4 million, reports the Latest York Post. Suter will make $3.75 million in 2026, and there's a $3.5 million club option for 2027 with a $250,000 buyout. He is the fourth reliever the Yankees have signed this offseason, joining David Bednar (accepted qualifying offer), Tim Hill, and Jonathan Loáisiga.

    Industry observers note that with the bullpen mostly assembled, the Yankees figure to pivot to offense the rest of the offseason. They need a third base upgrade over Ryan McMahon and a right-handed hitting catcher to pair with the lefty-swinging Austin Wells. It seems likely the Yankees will go with Anthony Volpe at second base and Spencer Jones in center field, but those positions can be improved as well.

    Industry observers note that the Mets have agreed to a deal with free agent first baseman Paul Goldschmidt, reports the New York Post. It's a one-year deal worth $8 million, according to The Athletic. He will presumably pair with Jared Young in a first base platoon. We did not rank Goldschmidt, 39, among our top 50 free agents. He accepted a reduced role for the Yankees over the last two seasons and was a valuable clubhouse presence.

    In a recent development, at this point in his career, Goldschmidt is no longer an everyday player, but he remains a solid platoon bat. He hit .317/.402/.572 against lefties over the last two years, compared to .235/.271/.337 against righties. Goldschmidt can still play a nifty first base as well. The Mets received the worst first base production in the sport in 2027. Even late-career Goldschmidt should be an upgrade.

    After missing out on Tarik Skubal, the Blue Jays are now believed to be prioritizing Freddy Peralta, according to MLB Network. Toronto has a very good one-two punch in Dylan Cease and José Soriano. Behind them are Spencer Arrighetti, Cody Ponce (returning from a torn ACL), Trey Yesavage, and maybe Jake Bloss and Ricky Tiedemann. There's room for another starter, for sure.

    According to recent reports, peralta, Michael King, and Trevor Rogers are the best available free agent starters now that Skubal has signed. Rogers declined the qualifying offer and is attached to draft pick compensation, which perhaps makes King or Peralta more desirable. Any of the three would boost a Blue Jays rotation that has upside but not much in the way of reliability behind Cease and Soriano.

    The Dodgers are not expected to aggressively pursue pitching help after losing out on Tarik Skubal, reports The Athletic. They're comfortable letting things play out and seeing what shakes loose among second- and third-tier free agents. As much as the Dodgers would have liked to retain Skubal, they're in a spot where they didn't absolutely need him.

    Recent findings suggest that despite this year's biceps and knee injuries, Shohei Ohtani is expected to pitch next season. He'll join Tyler Glasnow, Roki Sasaki, Blake Snell, and Yoshinobu Yamamoto in the rotation. Emmet Sheehan, Gavin Stone, and Justin Wrobleski are next in line, with prospects Jackson Ferris and Christian Zazueta not far away. The Dodgers could use another starter but aren't desperate for one.

    The Mariners, Padres, and Phillies are among the teams interested in Red Sox outfielder Jarred Duran, according to MassLive. The Red Sox tendered Duran a contract at Friday's deadline and will now look to trade him. The Jake Bauers signing pushed Duran, who had a .266 on-base percentage in 2026, out of the regular lineup. A trade is the logical next step.

    Philadelphia and San Diego badly need outfield help and are obvious fits for Duran. Even if the Mariners manage to re-sign Randy Arozarena, they could use another outfielder, though Duran would be a less-than-stellar fit for a lineup that is already heavily left-handed. Regardless, it seems unlikely Duran will be with the Red Sox by the time Opening Day arrives.

    Sources indicate that the Blue Jays, Phillies, and Yankees are considered the favorites for Japanese slugger Teruaki Sato, reports MLB.com. The Cubs and Mets are believed to have interest as well. Sato primarily played third base for the Hanshin Tigers but is not regarded as a strong defender, and it is likely that he will play first base or a corner outfield spot in MLB.

    According to recent reports, this past season, Sato, 28 in March, hit .306/.383/.609 with 39 home runs and won Japan's Triple Crown. He is similar to Munetaka Murakami in that he has big left-handed power, swing-and-miss concerns, and defensive problems. Murakami is a much more patient hitter, however. Sato is an aggressive swinger and is unlikely to walk much or post a strong on-base percentage.

    The Blue Jays offered Tarik Skubal a nine-year contract in the $400 million range before he signed with the Mets, according to The Athletic. Meanwhile, the Dodgers never reached the point of making Skubal an offer, reports ESPN. Los Angeles was known to prefer a short-term, high-dollar contract to a long-term arrangement. Getting Skubal on such a deal always seemed unlikely.

    It has been revealed that as for the Padres, they put forth an offer in the $400 million range but with deferrals that would have lowered the present day value, reports the Newly introduced York Post. Skubal's contract with the Mets includes $30 million in deferred money, which will lower the present day value some, but not significantly. The exact deferrals in San Diego's offer are unknown.

    In a recent development, the Royals and left-handed reliever Caleb Theilbar are in agreement on a one-year deal, per ESPN. Theilbar, 39, was excellent for the Cubs in 2025, but took a step back in 2026, pitching to a 4.86 ERA (87 ERA+) and 1.30 WHIP with 60 strikeouts in 50 innings pitched. He did strand 18 of the 23 runners he inherited, which is an adequate clip for a middle-relief type.

    The Royals recently acquired late-inning lefty José Ferrer in a trade and Daniel Lynch remains in the bullpen, so Thielbar could well be their third option as a lefty in relief.

    • There is an obligation on all of us, from supporters to pundits and journalists, to remain calm and measured about footballers as young as Max Dowman.
    • Recent findings suggest that "The hype will only continue to grow!"Max Dowman that is delightful!
    • It has been revealed that at this rate, Arsenal supporters will be looking forward to Carabao Cup matches as eagerly as any Premier League or Champions League game, simply because it will be a chance to watch Dowman again.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    There is an obligation on all of us, from supporters to pundits and journalists, to remain calm and measured about footballers as young as Max Dowman. But, my word, he does make it difficult. Arsenal’s 16-year-old sensation continues to sparkle whenever he steps on to the field, and he did so again with this superb display against Ipswich Town.

    Recent findings suggest that "The hype will only continue to grow!"Max Dowman that is delightful! 👏 pic.twitter.com/UfFY1VSyXn.

    It has been revealed that at this rate, Arsenal supporters will be looking forward to Carabao Cup matches as eagerly as any Premier League or Champions League game, simply because it will be a chance to watch Dowman again. The forward’s age and inexperience means he is still used sparingly in those high-priority competitions. The League Cup, by contrast, may prove to be his domain over the coming months.

    Dowman’s double at Portman Road made him just the second 16-year-old to score two goals in a game for a Premier League side. The first was Wayne Rooney, for Everton against Wrexham in 2002.

    Sources indicate that the two goals underlined why there is so much excitement around Dowman. The first was a demonstration of his prodigious dribbling ability, as he weaved through Ipswich’s defence and buried his shot with the weaker right foot. The second revealed his composure: a slotted finish, rolled in with ease.

    Sources indicate that max Dowman nets his second of the game! 😍 pic.twitter.com/XRZ9GqZx3x.

    As Mikel Arteta approaches the point of signing a new contract in north London, one wonders how much the idea of developing Dowman will excite him as he looks to the future. Which manager would not want to coach a player of such natural ability? Which manager would not want to see how good he could be? The same is true of Marli Salmon, the 17-year-old defender who also impressed on Tuesday night.

    Recent findings suggest that “A joy to have him,” remarked Arteta of Dowman. “It’s remarkable. It’s something very natural for him. He can deliver those actions effortlessly, I would say. What we have to do is look after him. He is 16. You don’t see that in this league. In other leagues in Europe, that’s a totally different context.

    It has been revealed that “Having two teenagers playing for Arsenal at this level is so fulfilling. Because I’ve been there and just to be able to contribute to somebody’s career and dream, to be able to experience a game like tonight, is phenomenal. And yeah, medium and long term, we know that if they continue to develop in the way that they are, we are going to have two tremendous footballers.”.

    "He was brilliant, he made the difference - we need to look after him" 🌟Mikel Arteta indicates Arsenal need to "be really cautious" with 16-year-old Max Dowman after he scored twice in Arsenal's 4-2 win over Ipswich 🔴 pic.twitter.com/1msJAEkK8z.

    Dowman’s two goals, along with strikes by Noni Madueke and Mikel Merino, secured a comfortable victory for Arsenal against Premier League opponents. Ipswich scored a goal of their own, through Anis Mehmeti, but never seemed likely to cause the visitors too much bother. A late strike from former Arsenal player Chuba Akpom was only a consolation. “We found a way to fight back into it,” said Gary O’Neil. “Losing by two goals to them isn’t a dreadful effort.”.

    According to recent reports, dowman is already developing a trademark goal, of sorts. His first strike for the club, against Everton last season, came after he left an opponent face-down on the turf at the Emirates Stadium. He inflicted the same pain here upon poor Cédric Kipré, who tried to tackle the teenager in the seventh minute but ended up with a mouthful of grass.

    It was an image that encapsulated Arsenal’s dominance in the early exchanges, as was the sight of Madueke firing in the second. The chance came after Bruno Guimarães and Merino, majestic in midfield, had monstered Ipswich’s attempts to play out from the back. Merino was dominant throughout, winning tackles with steel and then spinning away opponents with style. “He’s unbelievable,” said Arteta.

    Sources indicate that arsenal’s long-term relationship with the League Cup is not a particularly healthy one. For a club of their stature, it is a source of mild embarrassment that they have not won this competition since 1993. They came close last season, reaching the final at Wembley, but were defeated by Manchester City.

    Given the depth of Arteta’s squad, Arsenal really should reach the final again. If this is a tournament for the B-team, at least in these early stages, then Arsenal probably have the best B-team in the country. They started this game without any of Bukayo Saka, Declan Rice, Martin Odegaard, and Kai Havertz but were still extraordinarily strong in midfield and attack.

    The only pre-match concern was their defence, which has been weakened by a couple of early-season injuries. Arsenal started with Salmon at centre-back and the teenager was in direct combat with the physical, sharp-elbowed threat of Ipswich striker Zian Flemming. He stood up to the challenge with determination and class.

    Recent findings suggest that ipswich had made 10 changes following their victory at Crystal Palace at the weekend, which was an indication of where the Carabao Cup sits in their priorities. They were able to get into Arsenal’s penalty area but never gave the impression they could really hurt the Premier League champions, apart from when Mehmeti converted Jack Clarke’s low cross.

    Sources indicate that akpom struck in the 91st minute to encourage O’Neil, but by then the game had been lost. Arsenal’s work, and indeed Dowman’s work, had been done.

    "He's 16 years old, and we have to be cautious of that" 💫Mikel Arteta reacts to an incredible performance from Max Dowman as Arsenal put FOUR past Ipswich 🔴Don't miss the Carabao Cup on @paramountplus 📺 pic.twitter.com/AIcAbMx6ub.

    On managing the hype that surrounds Dowman, Arteta said: “What we have to do is look after him. He’s 16 years old, you don’t see that in this league. In other leagues in Europe, that’s a totally different context, but in this league, with the demands... We need to make sure that every time we throw him in it’s in the right context with the right preparation.”.

    Conor Coady shares his thoughts on Arteta’s role in Dowman’s development:.

    "He'll know how to nurture him!" 🗣️Conor Coady says Mikel Arteta is the perfect manager for Max Dowman 👏 pic.twitter.com/YdgLxfKiOf.

    Industry observers note that asked about Dowman’s two-goal performance, Arteta stated: “A joy to have him, Marli [Salmon] as well. Seventeen years old, to play at that level with the physicality they have to be able to handle that level, it’s remarkable. Max, yeah, it’s inevitable to talk about him when he scores and he creates the moments he has created tonight. It’s normal.”.

    He added: “He is coping better and better and better, he did the action where he regains the ball and wins it in the first goal, he loses his man... He’s an unbelievable player because of the character that he has and how much he loves to play on the biggest stage and still handles the situation with such naturality.”.

    Industry observers note that speaking in his post-match press conference, Mikel Arteta noted: “Really pleased with a lot of things we did tonight, the way we attacked the game, how dominant, fluid and aggressive we were, right from the beginning to try to influence the result. We scored two very early goals that gave us obviously a great platform for the game.

    In a recent development, “Individually some big performances as well. Some debuts tonight which is great to see as well, so we take a lot of positives from tonight.”.

    💡 Key Takeaways

    • In a recent development, bucks fans are supposed to stay standing until their team scores.
    • Lillard's return to the court where he tore his Achilles a little more than a year ago -- which came just one night after the Bucks faced Giannis Antetokounmpo for the first time -- was yet another reminder of how wrong things have gone in Milwaukee over the last few years, and the grim future the franchise faces.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that MILWAUKEE -- "Stay up! Stay up!" The pleading voice of the Milwaukee Bucks' in-arena host was still echoing around a half-empty Fiserv Forum early on Thursday night when Damian Lillard knocked the ball away from Tyler Herro and coasted the other way for the first points of a 124-114 Portland Trail Blazers victory.

    In a recent development, bucks fans are supposed to stay standing until their team scores. Those who are still proud enough to show up and follow the tradition get much more time on their feet than they did when Lillard was still in a Bucks jersey. They waited nearly two minutes on Thursday, then spent the next two hours watching Lillard pour in a season-high 33 points to send the Bucks to their 12th consecutive defeat and an NBA-worst 1-15 record.

    Lillard's return to the court where he tore his Achilles a little more than a year ago -- which came just one night after the Bucks faced Giannis Antetokounmpo for the first time -- was yet another reminder of how wrong things have gone in Milwaukee over the last few years, and the grim future the franchise faces. Jrue Holiday's 22 points, seven assists and four steals on Thursday only added to the misery.

    Industry observers note that trail Blazers coach Micah Nori joked pre-game that this might be the "first and only revenge game" of Lillard's career. Afterward, Lillard, who was waived by Milwaukee mere weeks after his injury, downplayed its significance. It was just a normal game, he said, "other than it just being the first time that I've played on the court since I got hurt.".

    Recent findings suggest that lillard's aggressiveness may have suggested otherwise, but both he and Nori attributed his approach to the Blazers being without Deni Avdija and Ja Morant. "When you're down your next two top scorers, I knew that I would need to be a little more assertive," Lillard noted.

    No one knew what to expect from the 36-year-old Lillard this season after such an extended layoff, but through 15 games he's averaging 20.9 points and 4.1 assists, and shooting 35.8% from 3-point range.

    "He still has the stop and go, which has made him so effective. Obviously, the jumper and his legs. I think the biggest difference would be, 18 months without playing, I don't know if you want to call it rust or timing, that's the only thing you see," Nori said pre-game. "And it's coming back. Every single day, you can see it. But when you're playing against the best athletes in the world, the best players in the world, the best defenders in the world, it is gonna take you a little bit of time to get back up to speed. But as far as from a health standpoint, you really wouldn't know it.".

    In a recent development, the moment Lillard's Achilles snapped 572 days ago during Game 4 of a first-round playoff series against the Indiana Pacers, everyone knew it was a turning point for the Bucks. But no one could have foreseen everything that's happened since then.

    The Bucks waived Lillard not even two months after the injury and stretched the remaining $113 million on his contract over five years in order to create the cap space to sign Myles Turner to a four-year, $107 million deal with a player option for the 2028-29 season.

    "I thought it was pretty simple. I was injured. I wasn't gonna be available to play last season, and the team was focused on bringing somebody in here that they could pair with Giannis so that they could still be a competitive team, which is the business side of it," Lillard stated Thursday morning at shootaround. "I saw it for what it was, and I moved on.".

    The desperate ploy to keep Antetokounmpo happy didn't work. Now, both he and Lillard are gone, while Turner is averaging just 7.1 points and six rebounds on 36.2% shooting this season and the Bucks are still paying Lillard $22,516,603 each year through 2030. If you break that figure down by game, they gave Lillard $247,592 for the trouble of beating them on Thursday while Turner sat and watched with a shoulder injury.

    Five years ago, Antetokounmpo and Holiday were carrying the Larry O'Brien trophy through the streets of Milwaukee. Three years ago, Holiday was traded for Lillard. Just over a year ago, Lillard tore his Achilles in the most recent playoff game at Fiserv Forum and was waived. Now, Antetokounmpo is leading the 9-6 Miami Heat, who sit in fourth place in the Eastern Conference, while Holiday and Lillard are together in the same backcourt for the 10-5 Trail Blazers, who occupy sixth in the Western Conference.

    And the Bucks, who haven't won a playoff series since 2022 and don't own their own first-round pick until 2031, the year after they'll stop paying Lillard? They're 1-15, have the worst record in the league and are in the midst of the second-longest losing streak in franchise history. Oh, and they're also under investigation for salary cap circumvention relating to Gary Trent Jr.'s $64 million contract.

    No team has a bleaker present or future than the Bucks.

    Industry observers note that just how bad are the vibes in Milwaukee? Major Goolsby's, a sports bar down the street from the arena, has started running a new promotion on game nights: everything's free if the Bucks win.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that the Chicago Cubs are signing free-agent left-handed starter Trevor Rogers to a five-year, $120 million contract, ESPN reports. He'll now frontline a Cubs rotation bereft of arms after Matthew Boyd, Shota Imanaga, Kevin Gausman, Clay Holmes and David Peterson all left via free agency this winter. Justin Steele, Cade Horton and Ben Brown, meanwhile, are all working their way back from injuries.

    Rogers, who recently turned 29, is coming off a solid campaign for the Baltimore Orioles in 2026:.

    According to recent reports, earlier in the offseason, CBS Sports ranked Rogers as the No. 3 overall free agent of the 2026-27 class and the second-ranked starting pitcher behind Tarik Skubal. Here's part of our write-up:.

    "Rogers was never able to fully work off the early season stinkers that inflated his ERA, though this is free agency, and ERA is close to the last thing on the minds of interested teams. You're looking forward in free agency, not backward. The underlying performance indicators are very strong, specifically the ability to get chase and avoid the barrel with four pitches (four-seamer, sinker, changeup, sweeper) that light up analytical models. Rogers also has a fifth-pitch cutter and has shown the ability to hammer the strike zone the last two years. There are some lefty Zack Wheeler vibes here. When Wheeler became a free agent after 2019, he already had the analytical stamp of approval, and the belief was he could get to another level with fine-tuning and good health. That is exactly what happened. Lefty Wheeler would obviously be the best-case scenario outcome for Rogers, but the bottom line is he will play the entire 2027 season at age 29, and he throws strikes with four pitches that the pitch data models already consider above average. More than a few teams will undoubtedly see Rogers as a pitcher who is a tweak or two away from finding another gear.".

    Rogers took the next step in 2025, and in the 38 starts he's made since the start of that season, he's put up an ERA+ of 128, an FIP of 3.20, and a K/BB ratio of 3.82.

    The Orioles made a qualifying offer to Rogers after last season, which means they'll be entitled to a compensatory draft pick now that he's signed elsewhere.

    Industry observers note that behind an offense backed by unanimous National League MVP Pete Crow-Armstrong and an elite defense, the Cubs made it to the Wild Card Series before being swept by the Padres, but their pitching, both starting and bullpen, wasn't up to the task. Now, with effectively a blank slate, the Cubs are expected to be in the market for multiple starting pitchers, and Rogers is the first domino.

    Rogers' contract is now the third-highest handed out to a Cubs pitcher, behind just Jon Lester (six years and $155 million) and Yu Darvish (six years and $126 million).
