    By HARRY BAMFORTH, LIVE SPORTS COVERAGE REPORTER.

    Published: 08:35 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 11:06 EST, 21 November 2026.

    Erling Haaland saw a first half equaliser controversially disallowed against Fulham, as Enzo Maresca's side only managed to fight back to earn a disappointing draw.

    Haaland latched onto a beautifully bent cross from Iliman Ndiaye to bundle home from less than eight minutes after Rodrigo Muniz had given the visitors a shock lead at the Etihad.

    But despite Bernd Leno appearing to fumble the ball over the line and the referee's watch flashing to signify a goal, the man in the middle ruled the equaliser out for a foul on the Cottagers goalkeeper.

    The decision has left both fans and pundits torn over whether the decision was harsh or whether it was the right call.

    Former Arsenal and Chelsea midfielder Karen Carney said her mind changed after having watched a replay of the incident.

    Speaking on TNT Sports from the Etihad, she mentioned: 'My initial reaction was I thought the goalkeeper didn’t have control of it, and it should've been a goal, but then when you slow it down, (you can see it).

    Sources indicate that erling Haaland has the ball in the back of the net, but it’s ruled out! ❌ 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max: https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB pic.twitter.com/sKqY8Q7a9Z.

    Erling Haaland has a first half equaliser for Man City chalked off against Fulham.

    Sources indicate that 'People are going to shout at me through the TV. But I think the referee made the right decision.'.

    Tottenham legend Glenn Hoddle, also on punditry duty in Manchester, felt the same.

    Industry observers note that he noted: 'I don’t know whether he had control of it, but I don’t think that comes into it. I think that’s the right decision, but it’s a very tough call. It could have gone either way.'.

    The Premier League Match Centre clarified why the decision was made by Tom Bramall and the VAR team in Stockley Park.

    A statement on social media read: 'The referee’s call of free-kick to Fulham and no goal to Manchester City was checked and confirmed by VAR – with the goalkeeper deemed to be in control of the ball.'.

    They added that the VAR stated: 'The ball is in control between both hands and then is played out of that possession by the attacker, and then into the back of the net.'.

    The laws of the game state that a goalkeeper is believed to be in control of the ball when the ball is 'between their hands/arms or between their hand(s)/arm(s) and any surface'.

    Not all fans, of a Manchester City persuasion or not, felt that the right decision was made. Some believed that both Haaland and City should feel hard done by.

    Haaland was left in disbelief by the referee's decision with many fans feeling the same.

    An Arsenal fan made their stance clear: 'Even as a rival, I honestly think this Haaland goal should’ve stood for Manchester City. Would’ve been p***** off if a Gyokeres goal like this for Arsenal was cancelled.'.

    In a recent development, A different fan added: 'Manchester City has been robbed. Haaland scored a clean goal here. The ball went in even before Haaland had contact with the keeper.

    Not everyone agreed, though, with many X owners taking the opposite stance.

    Recent findings suggest that one noted: 'It’s explicitly a foul under the Laws. Don’t blame the ref if you don’t like the laws.'.

    Industry observers note that another user wrote: 'I am also an Arsenal fan but the ball is still in two-palm contact. If you allow it, you will encourage outfield player challenging the save attempt And a foot to hand challenge will much more often lead to a broken wrist or thumb. That is an unfair advantage to outfield players.'.

    City did go on to equalise in the second half, with Elliot Anderson bagging his first Premier League goal for the club by smashing home a sublime volley in the 57th minute.

    #176186. Is Stephen Curry the real NBA MVP? It's hard not to think so when you watch the Warriors without him

    Is Stephen Curry the real NBA MVP? It's hard not to think so when you watch the Warriors without him

    📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1551 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It has been revealed that it's easy to forget because of what Stephen Curry has turned the Golden State Warriors into over the last decade and change, but this is an organization with some pathetic history in its books.
    • In a recent development, after battling admirably in a respectable loss to the Houston Rockets on the night Curry went down with an oblique injury in the first quarter, the Warriors have lost their last four games by 20-plus points for just the second time in franchise history.
    • Recent findings suggest that this current one is even worse.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that it's easy to forget because of what Stephen Curry has turned the Golden State Warriors into over the last decade and change, but this is an organization with some pathetic history in its books. So it's really saying something to start registering all-time marks of franchise ineptitude, which is precisely what the Warriors have done over the last week.

    In a recent development, after battling admirably in a respectable loss to the Houston Rockets on the night Curry went down with an oblique injury in the first quarter, the Warriors have lost their last four games by 20-plus points for just the second time in franchise history. The only other time this has happened to a Warriors team was in February of 1998, a few months after Latrell Sprewell choked P.J. Carlesimo. The total margin of that four-game losing streak was 104 points.

    Recent findings suggest that this current one is even worse. These Warriors have lost their last four by 109 points, and what makes it even more jarring is comparing them to the team that had won eight straight prior to Curry's injury. That 1997-98 team was trash all year, starting 1-14 and finishing with just 19 wins without ever winning more than three straight games.

    Sources indicate that these Warriors, on the other hand, were starting to look like a legitimate playoff-caliber team. A cynic would say that run of victories came against a softer schedule than what they have faced of late, but that qualification doesn't hold much, if any, water. That eight-game run included wins over the Denver Nuggets, Minnesota Timberwolves, Los Angeles Lakers, Miami Heat and an Orlando Magic team that has immediately gone on to win five of its last six.

    Perhaps the Warriors would have lost to the 13-3 San Antonio Spurs even with Curry. Hell, maybe they would've lost to the Fresh Orleans Pelicans, Dallas Mavericks and Memphis Grizzlies, too. That feels unlikely, but who knows? Even with Curry, the Warriors aren't good enough to start checking off scheduled wins. But that's not the point.

    The point is how utterly incapable they have looked in losing these games. Not only have they lost each of these last four by at least 20 points, but they've also been held under 100 points in all of them. That's a combination of incompetence that stretches beyond a franchise mark. That hasn't happened to a single other team this century.

    According to recent reports, before we try to answer that, let's just agree upfront that Curry has little to no chance of actually winning what would be his third MVP. The Warriors almost certainly won't have a good enough record to put him in real contention. His across-the-board counting stats, even if he were to maintain his torrid early pace, are not going to match those of Luka Dončić or Victor Wembanyama.

    The only real chance would be if both of those guys, and likely a bunch of others, failed to meet the 65-game threshold, but the chances of Curry, who has already missed six games and isn't expected to be re-evaluated until around Thanksgiving, making it to 65 games himself already feel next to impossible. He may be past the maximum 17 games-missed mark before he even returns from this injury.

    Sources indicate that which is to say, what we're asking here is whether Curry, at 38 years old and in his 18th season, is still the most valuable player in the league (has he always been?), not whether he'll actually win the award, and the answer to that question, at least in its simplest form, could very well lie in his absence. Just look at this team without him.

    Eight-game win streak with Curry.

    Four-game losing streak without Curry.

    In a recent development, admittedly, there's some cherry-picking in those numbers. Curry actually didn't play in one of the wins during that eight-game streak, and the Warriors still beat the Los Angeles Clippers 124-112 with a 122.8 offensive rating behind 37 points from rookie Yaxel Lendeborg.

    We're also leaving out the aforementioned game against the Rockets on Nov. 11 in which Curry only played six minutes and the Warriors looked fine, or even good, in testing one of the best teams in the league to its limit. It also must be noted that Golden State lost its first three games of the season and looked every bit like the team many of us predicted would stink, all of which Curry played in.

    Still, the general rule applies. The Warriors go as Curry goes. That was true even in the golden years when the on/off splits, even with the likes of Kevin Durant and Klay Thompson still out there, always pointed to Curry as the clear MVP.

    "If I didn't have Steph, I would've been like every other NBA coach and lasted a few years [with the Warriors] and then gone and coached somewhere else," Steve Kerr has said, openly admitting that Curry, and Curry alone, has been the difference between a journeyman coaching career and a Hall-of-Fame one.

    According to recent reports, he's not lying. Have a look at the numbers.

    Even if you want to remove the 2019-20 season from the equation, when Durant had defected, Thompson missed the whole year and Curry only played in five games, Kerr is still a below-.500 coach at 74-96 without Curry in the lineup. This is a coach who has had all kinds of great players at his disposal over the years, and still it was always Curry in control of his and the organization's ultimate fate.

    This is still the case for the Warriors, who continue to fall off a cliff without Curry. When he's been on the floor this year, they have registered a 59.6 eFG%, which would rank first in the league. When he's off, they fall to 49.1%, which would rank last.

    Even the defensive decline we see in Curry's on/off splits can largely be tied back to his offense. Without him, the Warriors are unable to create the same shots and, when their fresh brand of shots miss far more often, they end up defending in transition on almost 3% more possessions. That's a substantial deal. It's meant almost five more points per game surrendered to fast breaks over this stretch.

    Industry observers note that the Warriors have produced an average offensive rating of 103.8 in games Curry hasn't played this year, which would rank as the second-worst mark in the league. All told, they are 26.3 points per 100 possessions better in Curry's minutes this season, per Cleaning The Glass. By comparison, the Lakers drop by 25.5 points per 100 when Dončić sits. Wembanyama is in his own galaxy with this stat, representing a 37.8-point decline in San Antonio when he's off the floor.

    It's fair to say Wembanyama means as much to San Antonio's defense, where most of that decline happens, as Curry does to Golden State's offense, and certainly the Lakers falling off by as much as they do offensively, even with Austin Reaves as a legit secondary star, tells you everything you need to know about his impact. All of these guys are MVP players.

    But only one, by subjective definition, can be the most valuable, and the simple truth is the Lakers and Spurs are outfitted with far more functional rosters independent of their respective superstars. In Golden State, there is just nowhere else to turn. Nobody to generate any kind of consistent offensive leverage. No gravity. No shot creation.

    After the Warriors took that 38-point beating against the Spurs without Curry, the rookie Lendeborg, who had, in total unfairness, been saddled with filling Curry's go-to-scorer shoes, said "it felt helpless out there," and that is exactly what it has looked like since the Curry variable was removed from Golden State's equation.

    To be fair, the absence of a player is an imperfect lens through which to view value for a bunch of contextual reasons, not the least of which is how a team like Golden State is designed to play -- a specific, Curry-centric ecosystem not particularly amenable to abrupt adjustments. These players are not as bad as they have looked without Curry over these last four games.

    In a recent development, but by the same token, they aren't close to as good as they looked with Curry, either. I always laugh when my dad calls me saying things like, "This Pat Spencer guy can play!" Everyone looks like they can play next to Curry. And then he goes away and suddenly you're wondering how the hell this guy made the Washington Generals look like one of the best teams in the league. Is he some kind of miracle worker?

    In a basketball sense, that's not far off. Curry's individual production is already virtually unmatched, but it's his exponential powers, his ability to compound the returns of those around him, that set him apart. It's early, yes. Perhaps the Warriors will figure things out the longer Curry is away. Probably not. But maybe they at least can return to competitive functionality. Until then, however, it's pretty hard to not think Curry is the most valuable player in the league when you watch the Warriors play without him.

    Green Bay Packers coach Matt LaFleur confirmed Monday that running back Josh Jacobs is not expected to play in a crucial Thanksgiving Eve game against the Los Angeles Rams because of a finger injury he sustained in Week 9.

    Jacobs suffered the injury early in the Packers' beatdown of the Latest England Patriots and had surgery shortly thereafter. He had tried to re-enter the game but had trouble gripping the football.

    Running the ball has been a historic weakness for the Packers this year. Green Bay's 3.1 yards per carry is last in the NFL and on pace to be the worst by any team since the 2000 Chargers. The Packers are getting only 20% of their offensive yards on the ground, which is on pace to be the worst single-season mark since the 1970 AFL-NFL merger.

    Jacobs missed the first six weeks of the season while on the commissioner exempt list after being charged with two misdemeanors stemming from a May arrest. He scored three touchdowns in three games, but his 2.2 yards per carry is actually the worst of Green Bay's running backs. It's been a mess all year, both in runners and blockers.

    Recent findings suggest that the running game once again projects to be a major mismatch for Green Bay. The Rams' defense ranks 10th in yards per carry allowed overall but is first since Week 8, allowing just 2.9 yards per carry. As such, Jordan Love and wide receivers Christian Watson and Matthew Golden figure to carry a heavy burden.

    It has been revealed that kaleb Johnson, who played well in Jacobs' place after he left the Patriots game, could project to see the most early-down touches, though the rotation is convoluted. MarShawn Lloyd and Chris Brooks may see more passing-down work.

    This game is absolutely critical for both teams, as the Packers and the Rams are both 6-4. According to CBS Sports forecasting and projections, the Packers currently have a 38% chance to make the playoffs, while the Rams are right behind them at 35%. Green Bay's postseason chances would jump to 60% with a win; Los Angeles' would improve to 48% with a victory.

    According to recent reports, they scored. Would you believe it? Tottenham Hotspur, the team with more zeroes than an England Ashes batting collapse, found the back of the net but still frustration persists for Roberto De Zerbi.

    It could have been something different. The sight of the Italian dashing down the touchline in hailstones, grabbing his head in disbelief in the final seconds, showed this was not a straightforward tale of misery but, ultimately, the misery endures.

    It has been revealed that “I think this is five or six games we have been for sure not lucky,” De Zerbi lamented, but sympathy did not extend too far. Liverpool deservedly moved into the next round of the Carabao Cup, the gloss on Andoni Iraola’s most enjoyable night provided by Dominik Szoboszlai’s goal-of-the-season contender.

    THAT'S MAGNIFICENT! 💥🔴Outrageous strike from Dominik Szoboszlai 👏👏👏 pic.twitter.com/meQ7nilsz6.

    According to recent reports, yes, they went down swinging, as their noisy fans demanded. But carelessness cannot be excused and while De Zerbi complained about bad luck, a bad miss from Lucas Bergvall in the 10th minute was the fork in the road for the tie. Tottenham stalled and Liverpool never looked back.

    “We have to shoot more times and we have to shoot better,” De Zerbi harrumphed. “We have to finish better the clear situations. We are sorry for the result, disappointed and frustrated. I think it was unfair but we have to be stronger in these unlucky moments.”.

    Rather than fizzing his drive into the net, Bergvall succeeded only in firing straight at Giorgi Mamardashvili, when he had the whole target in front of him. It was, in all fairness, a brilliant save but he should never have been allowed to make it.

    For all the money that has been lavished by this club over the past 14 months, the one thing that the locals buy into more than anything is the basics done properly: hard work, tackling, a refusal to take second best. Iraola did not want Koumas to go anywhere this summer and it was obvious why.

    Sources indicate that “I see him training every day,” Iraola said. “He knows very clearly what he needs to do, what the team needs. And also the energy he shows is contagious for the rest. When you see the runs up front, giving everything, you are kind of forced to go behind and use the same intensity levels.”.

    It has been revealed that simple tenacity enabled Liverpool to get back on an even keel and laid the foundation for them to take the lead.     Whether it was the winger or Destiny Udogie, who was sliding to make a challenge, that ended up playing the ball to Alexis Mac Allister is immaterial, all that mattered is that the Argentine effortlessly placed his shot into the top corner, leaving Martin Dubravka planted and helpless.

    What De Zerbi would do to have a player in such form, but Tottenham are a skittish bunch, not the type of team who respond well in the face of adversity and their head coach, dressed in black with his oversized white trainers, regularly shook his head in exasperation.

    Industry observers note that his mood was not helped just before the interval, when Mohammed Kudus blasted over from eight yards following a zipped-in cross from Udogie, but he would not have called it truthfully if he had suggested Tottenham deserved parity at that stage. Soon Liverpool’s advantage would be doubled.

    The buffer they sought arrived in the 54th minute and, again, it was another genuinely attractive goal, with possession being kept until it sped up when Ngumoha scurried forward, found Milos Kerkez, who played it to Mac Allister, who in turn gave Gakpo the opening he craved.

    Recent findings suggest that his touch was excellent, his finish was even better and away in the distance Iraola rattled his fists in delight. That is two goals and four assists to start the campaign for the Dutchman and yet Liverpool were ready to sell him to Manchester City two weeks ago. What on earth were they thinking?

    Industry observers note that ruthless!! 🔥Cody Gakpo doubles Liverpool's lead against Spurs 🔴 pic.twitter.com/qlaaynMuwM.

    According to recent reports, from that point, it seemed inconceivable that Liverpool would finish living on their nerves, but De Zerbi’s decision to introduce Andy Robertson – given a hero’s reception on his first return to Anfield – and Mateus Fernandes wrestled back some impetus. There was also a significant helping hand.

    Unsurprisingly, Andy Robertson gets a great reception from the Liverpool fans on his return to Anfield 👏 pic.twitter.com/uNM6A00k5F.

    Mamardashvili had made some notable saves, including one from Kudus that he celebrated on his own, but he is vulnerable at set-pieces and Fernandes’s looping corner gave Conor Gallagher the easiest headed opportunity in three years to change the dynamic.

    Sources indicate that spurs have scored! ⚪️Conor Gallagher brings Roberto De Zerbi's side back into the game! pic.twitter.com/52zSCqClw4.

And as De Zerbi realised in the sodden conditions, with Tottenham it never rains. It only pours.

    A place in the League Cup fourth round is at stake at Anfield as Liverpool host Tottenham in an all-Premier League tie.

    Liverpool were frustrated on the weekend, being held to a 0-0 draw at home against Fulham, meaning they have one win and three draws from their opening four league games.

    Recent findings suggest that “I am very happy with the squad,” Liverpool head coach Andoni Iraola mentioned. “I value a lot my players, if we win games, the squad will look amazing and fantastic, if we do not there is going to be a problem with the depth. I think we will see also tomorrow [tonight] players we have not seen still and I am really looking forward to seeing. I feel they are going to play well and help us and they still have not had their chance. You can decide and put the same players in every game. The problem is there will be a moment when they are really tired. And there is more risk of injury.

    “But that is why we cannot say it does not work for anyone. There are players who play every three days with no issues. They are very robust, their performances do not change too much. There are other players where the risk is bigger and the performances are different. I have to learn who is ready to play games every three days and who needs a rest so their performance level is not affected. I thought I had it quite clear in my mind with some, but with others, it is latest, even for them, because they have not played as many games. We are learning.”.

    Sources indicate that liverpool were knocked out in the fourth round of this competition last season, losing 3-0 at home against Crystal Palace. Joe Gomez returns to the squad for the hosts tonight after an injury early in pre-season but Giovanni Leoni, Hugo Ekitike, Conor Bradley and Federico Chiesa remain out.

    Industry observers note that tottenham are still without a league win or goal this season. Their 0-0 draw at home against Everton Saturday means they sit just above the relegation zone. Tottenham overcame Charlton in the second round, convincingly winning 5-1 at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium last month.

    Industry observers note that “I think we are working well,” Tottenham boss Roberto De Zerbi mentioned. “We played 30 minutes, 25 minutes very well [against Everton]. In that moment we could score two goals. Then we lost maybe the confidence because we did not score. For sure we have to improve. For sure I have big confidence in my players, they are very good players.

    “We have to improve, yes. We can say the coach has responsibility if we do not score, yes, I accept, no problem. We did not win any game so far, yes. We are disappointed, sorry for that. But we have other positive things, like I said we did not [concede goals] in the last two games and the things we have to improve, we start our work. Nothing changed in my project and my idea.”.

    Tottenham’s League Cup journey last season came to an end in the fourth round last season, losing 2-0 at Newcastle. Sandro Tonali and Pedro Porro will not be involved tonight for the visitors and neither will Richarlison, who has been left out. Andrew Robertson returns to Anfield for the first time after leaving Liverpool in the summer following nine years on Merseyside.

    Breaking: Steelers' DK Metcalf denies trying to poke Eagles' Cooper DeJean in the eye

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (499 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • DK Metcalf claims that he wasn't intentionally trying to poke Cooper DeJean in the eye during an altercation that took place between the two during Sunday's game between the Steelers and Eagles.
    • Metcalf's encounter with DeJean led to his second unsportsmanlike conduct penalty of the third quarter, which ultimately resulted in his ejection.
    • "I just wish I would have been there for my team," Metcalf mentioned on Monday when asked about the incident.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    DK Metcalf claims that he wasn't intentionally trying to poke Cooper DeJean in the eye during an altercation that took place between the two during Sunday's game between the Steelers and Eagles.

    Metcalf's encounter with DeJean led to his second unsportsmanlike conduct penalty of the third quarter, which ultimately resulted in his ejection. Metcalf will surely be fined by the NFL and could possibly face a suspension as a repeat offender.

    "I just wish I would have been there for my team," Metcalf mentioned on Monday when asked about the incident.

    When asked about his struggles to keep his composure on the field at times, Metcalf said, "I think you got to ask the people that seem to do that to me.".

    Metcalf then corrected a reporter who alluded to his attempt to poke DeJean in the eye.

    "I didn't try to poke him in the eye," Metcalf said.

    Regardless, cameras did capture Metcalf poking his finger inside DeJean's facemask before the two were separated.

    DK Metcalf has been ejected in PhillyCBS | Paramount+ pic.twitter.com/johlxzOD1J.

    When asked about the incident on Sunday, DeJean said that Metcalf "almost" hit him in the eye but didn't.

    "You know, things like that happen in football," he mentioned. "It wasn't anything crazy; no one was really saying anything. It was just, you know, two guys going at it. He was trying to block me. I was trying to get him off of me. Things like that, and that obviously carried over to whatever that was at the end, or when he got thrown out.".

    According to recent reports, deJean mentioned that Metcalf's frustration may have stemmed from the fact that he had not had much impact on the game. Metcalf had just one catch for two yards prior to being ejected. He has six catches for 118 yards and one touchdown combined across Pittsburgh's last four games. His 3.6 receptions per game, 43.4 yards per game, and 5.9 yards per target would all either tie or set new career lows if the season ended today.

    Metcalf, however, does not attribute what happened Sunday to his lack of production.

    "No, I mean we're winning," he noted, before correcting himself. "We were winning.".

    Metcalf stated he doesn't know whether he will face further discipline from either the Steelers or the NFL.

    "You gotta ask Omar (Khan) that, or anybody else other than DK," he remarked.

    Metcalf, who served a two-game suspension last season after getting into an altercation with a Lions fan, was fined nearly $12,000 earlier this season for an unnecessary roughness penalty that was assessed during Pittsburgh's Week 4 loss to Cleveland.

    It has been revealed that metcalf has been fined over $750,000 by the NFL over his career between the suspension, multiple unsportsmanlike conduct penalties and other infractions, according to Spotrac. That number will surely rise in the coming days. And, as noted above, Metcalf could also be suspended for Pittsburgh's Black Friday game against the Denver Broncos.

    Breaking: In a New York minute: Did Mikal Bridges just turn his season around with one shot?

    📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (794 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Mikal Bridges was always up against a nearly impossible standard in New York.
    • Recent findings suggest that bridges entered Saturday's game against the Trail Blazers averaging 7.5 points per game on putrid 40/30 shooting splits.
    • Recent findings suggest that he's been showing signs of life of late.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Mikal Bridges was always up against a nearly impossible standard in New York. The Knicks sold everything but their soul to get him. He went from zero to hero over last year's championship run, then right back down to zero to start this season.

    Recent findings suggest that bridges entered Saturday's game against the Trail Blazers averaging 7.5 points per game on putrid 40/30 shooting splits. The familiar chatter was growing louder. Trade him. Or at least bench him. The Knicks entered Saturday having lost Bridges' minutes by a starter-worst five points per 100 possessions this season, per Databallr, and worse, they were +17.8 with him on the bench.

    Recent findings suggest that he's been showing signs of life of late. He went for 18 on 8-of-12 shooting against Indiana a week ago. He put up 17 on 7-of-11 in a win over the Raptors on Tuesday. The Knicks entered Saturday having won three straight and seven of their last nine.

    Make that four straight and eight of 10 as the Knicks stunned the Blazers 97-96 -- with Bridges turning his ever-extreme dial from zero all the way back up to hero with the shot that just may have turned his season around.

    Mike Breen doesn't bring out the double-bang often, but he did it on Saturday when Bridges took an inbound pass at the top of the key and, with the Knicks down two and 3.2 seconds on the clock, dribbled left and pulled up for the second buzzer-beater of his career (both of which have come against the Blazers).

    MIKAL BRIDGES HITS THE @TISSOT BUZZER-BEATER AS THE KNICKS WIN THEIR FOURTH STRAIGHT!🚨⏰ Everyone Gets 24 pic.twitter.com/UmtE1mOLRu.

    This would've been a gut-punch loss for the Knicks, who were on the verge of fumbling a 23-point halftime lead. Instead, as it turned out, it couldn't have been scripted better. Bridges needed a moment like this.

    It has been revealed that mike Brown hasn't pulled him from the starting five, but he only played him for 17 minutes in two straight games less than two weeks ago, and Bridges' minutes, largely as a result of that stretch, are down to a career-low 26 a game, which is the same burn Landry Shamet gets. This Nov. 15 portrait of basketball depression just about summed up the state of Bridges' season at that point.

    Mikal Bridges and Jose Alvarado on the bench. 😕(h/t @IQfor3) pic.twitter.com/0UU7J4Fd2v.

    Fast forward to Saturday night, when Madison Square Garden came alive with more than 50 franchise legends in the building for Homecoming Night, and this is what you call a vibe shift.

    KNICKS LEGENDS REACT TO MIKAL BRIDGES' @TISSOT BUZZER-BEATER 🔥 https://t.co/drFU31goFh pic.twitter.com/8HxH5Avnww.

    "When, quote-unquote, you think he's struggling, he just keeps playing," Brown said of Bridges after Saturday's game. "He doesn't let anything impact him. ... He's not going to get too high, he's not going to get too low. He's been there and done that. So for him to have the ball in his hands at that point in the game, there's a lot of confidence not only coming from him but from his teammates and the staff.".

    According to recent reports, in the interest of not totally overreacting to one shot, let's keep some perspective on this. Bridges only had 12 points vs. Portland. The Knicks still lost his 28 minutes by six points, the worst plus-minus of the night. But he made five of his eight shots and established a confident early rhythm.

    Industry observers note that bridges certainly hasn't been setting the world on fire, but for the most part he's been looking more like himself after a terrible start. The Knicks are now -49 for the season in Bridges' minutes, but they were -50 over the first three games, meaning he has been a net neutral since. That's nothing to celebrate, but it's not as bad as the prevailing perception.

    Now look at it the other way. The Knicks are +140 without Bridges on the court this season and, while there's no denying his contribution to that number with too many nothing offensive showings, understand that nearly half of it comes from two games (-24 against the Nets on Nov. 2 and -36 against the Bucks on Nov. 11).

    This isn't to suggest Bridges has been anywhere close to good so far. It's just to say that small samples can look like bigger deals than they are, and generally speaking, he's been slowly coming around. Maybe he just needed one game, one shot, one moment to reroute his basketball brain back toward the space he left it in as a playoff hero. Maybe Saturday night was that moment. Like the great Don Henley noted: In a New York minute, everything can change.

Justice Hill fumbled 1 yard from the end zone. LaJohntay Wester muffed two punts, one of which the Panthers recovered. Derrick Henry also lost a fumble. It's been a season from hell.     #176179. Dwight Howard admits he told Magic not to trade for Stephen Curry before he became 'one of the greatest'

    📅 22 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (971 w)

    Dwight Howard admits he told Magic not to trade for Stephen Curry before he became 'one of the greatest'

    📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (971 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, it is exceedingly rare for teams to have a chance to trade for one of the greatest players in NBA history.
    • The exception to this, bizarrely, has been Stephen Curry.
    • Industry observers note that there have been various levels of denial involved in all of these rumors, and we'll never really know all the details, but again, it's not as though we hear about this many botched deals for most of Curry's contemporaries.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, it is exceedingly rare for teams to have a chance to trade for one of the greatest players in NBA history. There were never serious rumors, for instance, about LeBron James or Michael Jordan getting traded. Magic Johnson and Kobe Bryant both issued public trade demands, but pulled back before a deal was consummated. Players like this, for the most part, don't make it to the rumor mill because nobody ever thinks they're seriously available.

    The exception to this, bizarrely, has been Stephen Curry. Though the rumors all died once he hit his prime, there is a rich history of teams that nearly traded for the greatest shooter of all time before he became, well, the greatest shooter of all time. At least three notable deals were reportedly scuttled at the finish line:.

    Industry observers note that there have been various levels of denial involved in all of these rumors, and we'll never really know all the details, but again, it's not as though we hear about this many botched deals for most of Curry's contemporaries. Of course, Curry differs from those contemporaries in one key way: he was not a sure thing. James came into the NBA as a preordained star. Anyone claiming they knew what Curry was going to become is almost certainly lying. There was quite a bit of doubt about him early in his career, and that doubt informs our latest entry into the Curry trade chronicles.

    In a recent development, dwight Howard appeared on the AM Hoops Show on Saturday and shared something few would be eager to admit: he told his former team, the Orlando Magic, not to trade for Stephen Curry. "I wanted to play with Monta Ellis and the Magic wanted to get Steph. The Magic wanted to get Steph and I remarked no. I said no because I didn't know. I didn't know Steph Curry was going to be one of the greatest," Howard said, regretfully. Asked specifically if the Magic came to him with this, he confirmed. "At the time, Monta was the one who was playing all the minutes," he added.

    In a recent development, howard did not offer a specific trade proposal or window of time when this could have happened, but two options come to mind. The first would be during the 2010-11 season, when Orlando revamped its team in mid-December by making two blockbuster deals that sent Vince Carter, Rashard Lewis, Marcin Gortat and Mickael Pietrus out while bringing back Gilbert Arenas, Hedo Turkoglu, Jason Richardson and Earl Clark. This would make sense as a period of roster transition, and Ellis was the league leader in minutes that season, averaging more than 40 per game across 80 appearances.

    According to recent reports, but Curry was no slouch that season when it came to availability either. He appeared in 74 games and averaged nearly 34 minutes. His availability didn't become a major concern until a year later, when ankle injuries limited him to just 26 games. At that point, his trade value would have been at its lowest, and Howard's leverage with the team would have been at its height. Howard had a player option for the 2012-13 season that he surprisingly exercised... even though the Magic didn't acquire Ellis. Orlando still wound up trading Howard to the Los Angeles Lakers in the summer of 2012.

    On paper, Curry was perhaps the perfect guard to pair with Howard at his peak. Of course, Curry was and remains the perfect player to pair with just about anyone, but Howard, specifically, tried and failed to mesh with two high-usage star guards in Kobe Bryant and James Harden. Curry's eagerness to play off of the ball would have allowed Howard more post-up possessions, a priority of his at the time even if such plays didn't represent great offense. The team could have run through Howard, but still benefitted enormously from the young Curry's presence before eventually shifting in Curry's direction as Howard aged out of his physical prime.

    Stan Van Gundy was a pioneer in the 3-point revolution, building a four-out lineup around Howard with players like Lewis and Turkoglu. It's tempting to think about what he could have done with a young Curry, especially since Van Gundy would miss another chance to coach him down the line, when he elected to take the Detroit Pistons job in 2014 rather than continuing to pursue Golden State's vacant position.

    But if there ever really was a window for someone to swoop in and steal Curry, it closed after that third, injury-plagued season. Curry broke out in the 2012-13 season by leading the Warriors back to the playoffs, made his first All-Star team a year later, and then a year after that, he won the first of his two MVP awards and four championships. From that point forward, Golden State had no reason to ever entertain the notion of trading Curry, and Howard, like the Suns, Hornets and Bucks, was left to wonder about what might have been.

    According to recent reports, ironically enough, Howard would get another chance to pair up with Curry in 2013, after Curry had proven himself as Golden State's lead guard. He was a free agent that offseason and met with the Warriors, but seemingly preferred Harden as his running mate, as he signed with the Houston Rockets. The Warriors turned around and used their cap flexibility to add dynasty mainstay Andre Iguodala, an essential part of a team that largely won without high-profile centers like Howard. With the benefit of hindsight, Howard might be one of the most crucial hidden figures in Golden State's rise to prominence. If he had any inkling of the sort of legend Curry was destined to become, the Warriors dynasty may never have happened.

    Industry News: U21 European Championship Final: English Manipulation of the German Pressing – MH

    📅 06 Jul 2025 | ⏱️ 12 min read (2417 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Spielverlagerung

    ⏱️ ~12 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • von Next Generation am 06.07.2025 in den Kategorien National Teams mit 1 Kommentar.
    • England wins the U21 European Championship final against Germany 3-2.
    • The U21 European Championship final offered several interesting tactical elements.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    von Next Generation am 06.07.2025 in den Kategorien National Teams mit 1 Kommentar.

    England wins the U21 European Championship final against Germany 3-2. After just 20 minutes, England leads 2-0. This aspect analysis focuses on the reasons behind the German attacking press’s lack of access to England’s build-up play.

    The U21 European Championship final offered several interesting tactical elements. This analysis focuses on Germany’s lack of access in their attacking pressing and marking. Particularly in the first half, England repeatedly managed to bypass the German press, often gaining large amounts of space in the final third, which led to dangerous scoring opportunities.

    The early deficit also contributed to Germany being unable to focus, as they usually do, on securing depth in their pressing. Instead, they were forced to put direct pressure on the ball carrier in order to force turnovers. After the equalizer to make it 2-2, Germany noticeably pressed high less frequently. Therefore, this analysis examines Germany’s pressing and marking, as well as England’s build-up play, up to the 60th minute.

    Sources indicate that one of the trends at the U21 European Championship was that many teams aimed to press the opponent’s goal kicks with a +1 player on the last line or in the space between the lines just in front of the back line. Many teams—including Germany—used man-oriented marking when closing down during goal kicks.

    Since most teams build up from a 1-4-2-4 structure on goal kicks, it is equally common to press man-to-man from a 4-1-3-2 shape, with the two holding midfielders (the “sixes”) staggered vertically.

    It has been revealed that the deeper-lying holding midfielder (for Germany: Martel) acts as the +1 player, positioning himself in space based on the location of the ball. When the opponent plays through the space between the lines, he can create a numerical advantage there. In the final third, pressing is carried out against a 1-4-2 build-up using a 3-2 shape. The more advanced holding midfielder (for Germany: Reitz) typically positions himself centrally and marks the ball-near holding midfielder, while the far-side winger presses the ball-far holding midfielder.

    It has been revealed that the English side, by contrast, caused problems for the German team’s marking assignments through an asymmetrical structure. As a result, England had several options for exploiting their numerical superiority in the build-up without having to immediately play into the space between the lines.

    What remained consistent was the intention to establish central possession in front of the first pressing line using different players, in order to build up play on either side. Central possession makes it more difficult for the pressing team to steer the play in a specific direction, as the passing angles from central areas are wider than those from more advanced or wider positions.

    Recent findings suggest that central possession complicates the opponent’s shaping of play. Anderson’s drop frees him from Woltemade’s marking shadow and creates a numerical advantage against Nebel, who must now cover both the advanced full-back and Anderson.

    The asymmetry in England’s build-up play also allowed them to repeatedly exploit their numerical superiority in specific areas tailored to Germany’s pressing structure. By stretching the positioning of their two holding midfielders (the “sixes”), Reitz was forced to cover too much ground to mark both or to shift swiftly to the ball-near midfielder.

    Because Germany, for the reasons mentioned above, struggled to steer the press in a specific direction, Reitz was also unable to position himself closer to the ball-near player during goal kicks. Instead, he was forced to choose which of the two midfielders to mark man-to-man.

    The wide, asymmetric positioning of the holding midfielders and advanced full-backs makes both midfielders available for passes, forcing Reitz to choose whom to mark. German forwards can’t shadow the opposing midfielders, while German wingers must decide between marking the spaced-out midfielders or full-backs.

    Recent findings suggest that england’s positional rotations during build-up play after goal kicks were most often initiated by holding midfielder Anderson. When Germany applied pressure (as shown in the diagram above), Anderson would frequently drop into the right half-space, almost into a right-sided centre-back position, while fellow holding midfielder Scott positioned himself more centrally, and No. 10 McAtee dropped into the higher left half-space.

    When Anderson instead dropped centrally in front of the goalkeeper, the right centre-back would shift wide, which in turn affected the positioning of other central players and full-backs. The specific rotations of the key players, including their reference points and triggers, are discussed in more detail in the section on England’s build-up against Germany’s high pressing.

    A key aspect of England’s build-up against Germany’s pressing was their ability to evade pressure through these rotations. Since Germany used man-oriented marking, they followed the English players during these movements, which repeatedly opened up spaces that England could then exploit. For example, when McAtee dropped deep into the far-side half-space, it pulled Martel—who was defending space-oriented in the center—out of position.

    Recent findings suggest that the aim was to repeatedly open up central areas by drawing German players out of the middle. When the full-backs, due to the rotations, were positioned deep and wide in possession, the ball-near holding midfielder would shift outward, thereby opening the central channel. This would often be followed by an overlapping run by the full-back into the half-space, allowing him to be found deep in the center with his marker behind him and plenty of space to operate.

    Industry observers note that luring central players out of position and opening up space through rotations is one of the core principles of England’s build-up play. It significantly disrupted Germany’s ability to gain access through their man-marking approach during pressing.

    Holding midfielder Anderson’s run outward opens the center, which can then be exploited by the full-back’s typical forward run.

    Industry observers note that england also added flexibility by repeatedly using long balls from their build-up play. Especially when both the full-backs and the holding midfielders were positioned deep, they opted for long passes as soon as Germany’s wingers and central players were lured far enough out. The 2–0 goal resulted from one such long ball, which was held up by striker Stansfield and laid off to the advancing Elliott and McAtee in the half-space, who now had plenty of room to operate in the open central area.

    In a recent development, although these long balls weren’t always as successful as in the lead-up to the 2–0, they had the effect of preventing Germany from pressing too aggressively, as players had to remain ready to cover depth in case of another long ball. For example, Martel pushed forward only hesitantly toward the dropping No. 10 McAtee, giving him significantly more time on the ball in central areas.

    Against man-oriented marking systems, it is particularly important to apply intense pressure on the ball carrier, since progression is otherwise easier than against a zonal setup.

    As described, England repeatedly managed to exploit their numerical advantage in the build-up. However, Germany’s pressing approach also contributed to their lack of access. The primary aim of Germany’s pressing when closing down is less about disrupting the build-up itself, and more about winning the ball in a way that immediately creates a transition opportunity.

    To do so, Germany tries to use its forwards to immediately block passing lanes to the flanks, forcing the play through the third man or central passes.

    In a recent development, recovering possession through intercepting a pass has the advantage over winning a tackle in that it tends to allow better control of the ball and therefore more often leads to a transition opportunity. Additionally, central ball recoveries naturally result in a shorter route to goal and, statistically, in higher-quality chances in front of goal.

    Recent findings suggest that however, this type of pressing also means less pressure is placed on the ball carrier, since the focus is on directing play and winning the ball after a pass. As a result, England’s ball carriers had more time to locate the free +1 player, made available through asymmetry and rotations.

    According to recent reports, in hindsight, it might have been more effective to place greater emphasis on actively disrupting the build-up itself, because England repeatedly managed to bypass the German press dangerously. At the same time, Germany had the ability to control the game through their own possession, so it wasn’t absolutely necessary to rely on winning the ball high up the pitch to create chances.

    In a recent development, germany’s attacking pressing operated on principles similar to those of their closing down (Zustellen). From a 4-4-2 formation with a slightly advanced Reitz on the left half-space, the forwards aimed to channel the opponent’s build-up play out wide in order to isolate the wide build-up players and engage them in man-to-man marking.

    It has been revealed that on the last defensive line, Germany aimed to maintain a +1 numerical advantage, which is why the far-side holding midfielder was usually responsible for covering depth. The German wingers were expected to track back from the full-backs to press the half-backs in the three-man defensive line that frequently formed.

    The exemplary German attacking press.

    Even when applying attacking pressing from open play, Germany was rarely able to gain effective access to England’s build-up. This was primarily due to England’s positional play during build-up. England’s main objective in possession is to lure opponents out of position and then exploit the spaces that open up. This goal is achieved through positional rotations that make it especially difficult for the opponent to apply effective pressure on the ball carrier during pressing. The frequency of these rotations strongly resembles the rotation-heavy positional play famously associated with Paris Saint-Germain.

    The following outlines the key running paths, rotations, and reference points of the most key players.

    The center-backs were rarely involved in the rotations. Only when one of the holding midfielders dropped into the build-up line did the center-backs position themselves wider. Likewise, striker Stansfield provided a fixed presence in the central deep-lying position.

    It has been revealed that most rotations initially originated from the holding midfielders, particularly Anderson. Most frequently, he dropped into the right half-space just ahead of the center-backs. This caused the right full-back to position wider and winger Elliott to drop deeper into the half-space at the level of the last defensive line. As a result, Woltemade and Nebel had to press two players, creating a 3 vs. 2 overload.

    There were also occasions when Anderson dropped into the central center-back position. Consequently, the full-backs rotated into the half-spaces, or No. 10 McAtee dropped deeper. Notably, Anderson could be found almost anywhere on the pitch. At times, he overloaded the far side, which was then followed by a role swap between him and holding midfielder Scott.

    Sources indicate that holding midfielder Scott often positioned himself in spaces that were left vacant after a sequence of rotations. Usually, Scott remained central or rotated roles with holding midfielder Anderson. It also happened that Scott took up an open full-back position when both the winger and the full-back rotated deep.

    A particularly noticeable tendency of both holding midfielders was that, when in possession, they rotated toward the flank if a wide player was positioned close to the first build-up line, making themselves available along the sideline. This had the advantage of stretching the center even further.

    According to recent reports, this was especially vital because England frequently won second balls after losing possession in build-up play. In the resulting transition situation, the central area was completely free, leading to several dangerous counter-attacks through the now open middle of the pitch.

    Livramento, as the right full-back, primarily oriented himself around Anderson and the right winger Elliott. In relation to Elliott, Livramento always behaved in a complementary manner: when one occupied the wide position, the other took up the half-space. It was also common for Livramento to invert and drop into the deeper half-space, with Elliott moving wider in response, and vice versa.

    According to recent reports, anderson served as a secondary reference point. Whenever Anderson dropped back to form a wide back three, Livramento either moved inverted or stayed wide and deep. If Anderson remained central, Livramento positioned himself near the center-backs in the half-space, from where he could rotate forward into depth if the outside lane was free.

    On the left side, full-back Hinshelwood and winger Hutchinson rotated according to the same principles as Livramento and Elliott. Hinshelwood also frequently inverted into the deeper half-space or moved wide and deep. Both full-backs, Livramento and Hinshelwood, often initiated rotations through their inverted runs when the ball was with the near-side build-up player.

    Runs into depth, however, were usually triggered only when other players moved to offer passing options. The No. 10 McAtee also played an important role as a reference point. When McAtee (and/or Hutchinson) moved into the left half-space, Hinshelwood rotated oppositely into depth.

    McAtee, as a left-sided No. 10, had a freer role. He oriented himself around the holding midfielders to occupy or overload the central area when needed. He also rotated positions with left winger Hutchinson. Often, McAtee initially moved far into the left half-space to pull defenders out of the No. 10 zone behind him and then sometimes rotated further back toward the central center-back position.

    Recent findings suggest that in response, either full-back Hinshelwood or holding midfielder Anderson rotated forward into depth. Alternatively, winger Hutchinson could rotate into the half-space, prompting full-back Hinshelwood to rotate wider.

    Recent findings suggest that the English rotations created difficult conditions for Germany’s man-oriented attacking pressing. Man-marking was repeatedly manipulated, which in turn stretched and opened up spaces. Thanks to the flexibility of long balls and superiority in second balls, England’s build-up play additionally benefited in the first half. This led to repeated situations resembling counter-attacks, as England had plenty of central space available after bypassing the press.

    According to recent reports, the early goal also forced Germany to press higher more frequently and reduced their tendency to drop deep. Germany’s pressing behavior against England’s build-up thus became one of the decisive factors influencing the course of the game in the first half.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Brandon Aiyuk's time in San Francisco has apparently come to an end.
    • The 49ers were given a two-week roster exemption when the NFL reinstated Aiyuk on Nov.
    • Industry observers note that aiyuk started the 2025 season on the PUP list.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Brandon Aiyuk's time in San Francisco has apparently come to an end. The 49ers have released Aiyuk, who will now look to continue his career with a new team, according to a report from ESPN.

    The 49ers were given a two-week roster exemption when the NFL reinstated Aiyuk on Nov. 9. With that exemption ending on Nov. 23, the 49ers elected to move on from Aiyuk, who hasn't played an NFL game since tearing his ACL and MCL during the 2024 season. Aiyuk had signed a four-year, $120 deal with the 49ers that offseason following a tumultuous negotiation. That contract, as currently structured, still has two years remaining, with a 2027 cap hit of $40.5 million according to Over the Cap, meaning Aiyuk will likely need to clear waivers before any team formally signs him.

    Industry observers note that aiyuk started the 2025 season on the PUP list. That November, it was reported that the 49ers voided the guaranteed money in his contract for 2026 due to lack of participation. In December, the 49ers placed him on their reserve/left squad list.

    It has been revealed that this summer, the 49ers placed Aiyuk on the reserve/did not report list (meaning the 49ers were not obligated to pay him and he did not count against their roster) after he did not report to training camp. Aiyuk had since applied for reinstatement with the NFL and was granted it earlier this month.

    Before 2024, Aiyuk enjoyed a productive career with the 49ers, who selected him with the 25th overall pick in the 2020 draft. In 2022, he eclipsed 1,000 receiving yards for the first time and caught a career-high eight touchdowns. The following season, he recorded a career-high 1,342 receiving yards while helping the 49ers reach the Super Bowl.

    While his recent actions in San Francisco might scare some teams off, Aiyuk will likely draw interest from teams that need help at receiver. Aiyuk has long been linked to the Commanders; he and Washington quarterback Jayden Daniels were teammates at Arizona State. The Steelers are another team that could potentially be a landing spot for Aiyuk.

    Despite not having Aiyuk, the 49ers are 9-1 and would be the No. 1 seed in the NFL if the playoffs started today.

    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that victor Wembanyama is hard to put into words.
    • So here we go again, trying to write about the indescribable Wembanyama, who put 50 points, 19 boards, five blocks and four steals on the Pelicans on Saturday.
    • Just take a look at this guy making the greatest basketball players in the world look like children.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that victor Wembanyama is hard to put into words. Stephen Curry is the only player I can remember thinking of the same way in the post-Michael Jordan era. Nobody else. With Steph and Wemby, you can't fully describe what you've seen. You try, but in the end you just have to see them to understand. It's totally different than anything you've ever witnessed on a basketball court.

    So here we go again, trying to write about the indescribable Wembanyama, who put 50 points, 19 boards, five blocks and four steals on the Pelicans on Saturday. It feels like we're qualifying one of his "first in history" stat lines about once a week, and indeed, Wembanyama is the first player since blocks and steals became an official stat in 1973 to record those single-game numbers.

    Just take a look at this guy making the greatest basketball players in the world look like children.

    VICTOR WEMBANYAMA BECOMES THE FIRST PLAYER SINCE 1973-74 TO RECORD 50+ PTS, 15+ REB, 4+ STL AND 5+ BLK IN A GAME!🤯 50 PTS🤯 18 REB🤯 5 BLK🤯 4 STL🤯 5 3PM🤯 32 MINSPURS WIN THEIR 14TH IN 15 GAMES. pic.twitter.com/lPKk3jYNjL.

    Before the halftime buzzer had even sounded, Wembanyama had already tallied 32 points, 13 rebounds, three steals and three blocks. That would be a career game for a lot of NBA players. He had played 18 minutes. You can only laugh at this point.

    What was even funnier, however, was Wembanyama's comment after the game, when he took a clear stab at, well, whoever he considers his "peers" to be by calling them out for, shall we say, unethical statistical pursuits.

    "It is very special," Wembanyama said of reaching the 50-point mark for the second time this season and third time in his career. "But unlike many of my peers, I'm not good at stat-padding. So I haven't reached it as many times as I should have.".

    Victor Wembanyama after scoring 50 points: “Unlike many of my peers, I'm not very good at statpadding.” pic.twitter.com/OAogFCa2oi.

    Recent findings suggest that so here's what's interesting about this little dig: Wembanyama was definitely guilty of stat-padding his way to 50 in this game. With just more than eight minutes remaining and the Spurs up by 24, Wembanyama could've stayed on the bench after the timeout. The Spurs have made a concerted effort to limit his minutes whenever possible this year. Even in the golden age of comebacks, this game was over.

    But Wemby stayed in and proceeded to take five straight shots on the next five possessions. He was hunting the 50. No question about it. He even admitted as much.

    "The greats of the game, they don't care [about stat-padding]," Wemby stated, via The Athletic. "I don't think Wilt [Chamberlain] thought about that when he had 98 points. ... That stepback 3, going right, that I took, it doesn't correlate with this. It didn't fit to the definition [of ethical basketball], for example. So I did try [to stat-pad] at the end.".

    Good on Wemby for acknowledging his own hypocrisy, but it raises the question: if you just did the very thing you are railing against, why take the jab in the first place? Every player who has been within range of 50 points has gone for it as long as it's not a competitive game in which quality shots still matter. It's not that big a deal.

    In a recent development, but Wemby has done this before. In December of 2025, after the Spurs had just defeated the Thunder, he noted, "I'm just glad to be part of something that's growing to be so beautiful — pure and ethical basketball.".

    According to recent reports, this was a definite jab at Shai Gilgeous-Alexander's foul-baiting. Wemby, meanwhile, has turned into one of the more theatrical floppers in the league. In almost every way, Wembanyama is different than any other basketball player in the world. But when it comes to this ethical, non-stat-padding basketball soapbox he has climbed upon on numerous occasions, the truth is he's just like everyone else. So enough with the jabs.

    • By TAMARA PRENN, SENIOR SPORTS REPORTER and LUKE AUGUSTUS, ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR.
    • Published: 02:49 EST, 18 November 2026 | Updated: 12:04 EST, 21 November 2026.
    • Mauricio Pochettino has issued a rallying cry to Manchester United supporters, promising that this is going to be a 'special season' despite their dismal start which sees them 18th in the Premier League with just one win from their opening 10 games.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By TAMARA PRENN, SENIOR SPORTS REPORTER and LUKE AUGUSTUS, ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR.

    Published: 02:49 EST, 18 November 2026 | Updated: 12:04 EST, 21 November 2026.

    Mauricio Pochettino has issued a rallying cry to Manchester United supporters, promising that this is going to be a 'special season' despite their dismal start which sees them 18th in the Premier League with just one win from their opening 10 games.

    The new Red Devils head coach landed in Manchester on Wednesday morning, hopping straight off a private jet to meet his new players, hours after leading the USA in his final game as their boss.

    And during a busy first day among his latest surroundings, the Argentine sent a direct message to the club's fanbase as he preached for unity.

    'Hi Reds, here's it's Mauricio Pochettino,' he remarked via a video posted on United's X account at 7.15pm on Wednesday evening.

    Sources indicate that 'I am looking forward to meeting you guys. I hear so many good things about you.

    'I hope we bring all the happiness working together and connecting together.

    A message from Mauricio 💬❤️🤳 #ShotOnSnapdragon pic.twitter.com/2lBLkMaGY6.

    Mauricio Pochettino addressed Manchester United fans directly on Wednesday evening after starting work officially as their new head coach.

    The new Red Devils head coach has promised a 'special season' in a direct message to fans.

    Pochettino poses at his unveiling with United director of football Jason Wilcox on Wednesday.

    'This is going to be a special season to support and to make our players to fight on the field and to get the results that we deserve.'.

    In a second message in his native Spanish, Pochettino expanded further: 'This message is about being united, like the name Manchester United. We all need to work together.

    'I hope to bring the happy moments that this club deserves and create the unity that every team needs so that the players can be at their best on the pitch.'.

    It has been revealed that those messages came less than eight hours after arriving in England. He landed in Manchester at 11.32am on Wednesday and immediately headed to their Carrington training base where he took a tour and met players and staff.

    Sources indicate that speaking to the club's media channels earlier on Wednesday, Pochettino said: 'Thank you so much, I'm very excited to be here. It's an honour, it's a privilege to be in this amazing club. I'm looking forward to starting work.'.

    The club then officially welcomed the newly introduced manager on their website, writing: 'Mauricio Pochettino has officially started work as Manchester United head coach, marking the start of a dream role for the Argentinian.

    Industry observers note that 'Pochettino is joined at United by a team of loyal staff he has worked with at Espanyol, Southampton, Tottenham Hotspur, Paris Saint-Germain, Chelsea and USA. Join us in welcoming Jesus Perez, Miguel D’Agostino, Toni Jimenez, Alec Scott and Sebastiano Pochettino.'.

    Pochettino had made a promise to end Man City's dominance as United manager in his last interview as United States national team coach on Tuesday evening.

    He took off from northern Kentucky in a private jet chartered by the club after his final match on American soil, which saw the US beat Haiti 2-0 in Cincinnati.

    But before becoming airborne, Pochettino had time for a final statement Stateside, after being taunted that 'Manchester is blue, and will always be blue' by one of his interviewers.

    Earlier on Wednesday, Pochettino made his way to Carrington straight after landing in Manchester, meeting players and staff and taking a tour.

    The Argentine took off from northern Kentucky in a private jet last night and landed at 11.32am.

    The manager shared a picture from his journey as he prepared to touch down at the airport (Source: Instagram/Mauricio Pochettino).

    Recent findings suggest that 'No way,' he shook his head. 'You will see.'.

    Industry observers note that 'Give me time. Give me time and then that - that's going to change.'.

    Pochettino also shared a poignant farewell message to his US set-up, days after breaking down in tears in a press conference ahead of his penultimate time in charge.

    Man United fans may also have been pleased to read of Pochettino's new-found love of John Denver's song Country Roads in his goodbye message, a song which is played before kick-off at Old Trafford.

    'It is never easy to say goodbye, especially after everything we experienced together.' Pochettino captioned a carousel of photos of his time in the role. 'I always wanted the opportunity to coach in the USA, and I was very happy to have this chance with the national team. Two incredible years, with so many great moments and experiences that will stay with me always.

    'From the challenges we faced at the Gold Cup to the excitement of the USA hosting the World Cup, and now finishing our time by reaching the semi-finals of the Nations League, I am proud of what we achieved.

    It has been revealed that 'When we arrived, I wanted us to believe that we could compete with anyone. I hope today that belief is stronger, not only with the players but with everyone who supports this team. Not everything in football can be measured by results, and I believe we have helped build something notable for the future of soccer in this country.

    The plane believed to be carrying Pochettino and his staff was hired by Manchester United.

    'This experience has re-energised me and given me so much, both in football and personally. I have discovered a wonderful country, made upcoming friends and enjoyed so many of the traditions. Every time I hear Country Roads, I will forever think of all of you with a smile.

    'Thank you to the players, staff, everyone at (the US national team) and all the supporters. Especially to those who believed in us and gave us this opportunity.

    'Leaving is tough at this moment, but sometimes in football an opportunity comes that is impossible to say no to. I have always believed in following my heart, even when it means leaving a place where I have been very happy.

    Industry observers note that 'I hope this team continues to grow and achieves all the success it deserves. Thank you USA.'.

    Pochettino had previously explained his emotions as stemming from how difficult the decision had been to leave the national team and re-start at Old Trafford.

    Sources indicate that ‘I haven't prepared a speech, I'm talking with my heart,’ he said on Friday. ‘It's difficult for me to talk now because I am a very emotional guy.

    Recent findings suggest that ‘When these moments arrive, it is always tough. Normally it is the opposite – you have been sacked! You cry because you want to stay.

    ‘I think it was one of the most difficult decisions of our career, but you have to move forward.

    ‘Not too many opportunities can happen in your career with a side like Manchester United. That is difficult to turn down when it arrives.

    ‘In some part it’s a very sad decision, in another part we are professional and we are trying to make our dreams come true. We are excited for that step forward.'.

    Man United first made contact with Pochettino following their breathless 4-4 draw against Aston Villa in their last match before the international break.

    The Man United hierarchy had previously given former head coach Michael Carrick a stay of execution amid a worrying start to the season, but as they prepared to head into the two-week pause in the relegation zone, the board became keen to make a change.

    An agonising wait for Carrick followed, with the club legend taking training for multiple sessions at the start of the week as his future was openly mulled by executives including CEO Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox.

    After the duo returned from Monaco, where they had flown to speak to co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe about Carrick's future, the 45-year-old was finally dispatched last Thursday morning.

    In their statement regarding Pochettino's arrival on Wednesday, United also confirmed the exits of Carrick and Co, writing: 'The club can confirm the departures of Travis Binnion, Jonny Evans, Steve Holland, Craig Mawson and Jonathan Woodgate alongside Michael Carrick.

    'We would like to thank the group for their total commitment, dedication and professionalism, and we wish them all good luck for the future.'.

    Pochettino's United States farewell match went off in pitch-perfect style, which allowed thoughts to swiftly move to the next task at hand after the final whistle.

    Christian Pulisic helped make sure that Pochettino's reign in charge ended on a high note.

    The manager will now focus his attentions on getting Man United out of the relegation zone.

    It has been revealed that 'When you finish the game, you start in your mind to think about different things,' Pochettino remarked after the win. 'Of course, it's tough because it's emotional. Because I really love these guys, and I love the players. I love the staff. I love the fans and everything.'.

    Travelling with Pochettino were outgoing USMNT first-team coach Miguel D'Agostino, strength and conditioning coach Silvia Tuya and analyst Alec Scott, while his assistant Jesus Perez, goalkeeper coach Toni Jimenez as well as Pochettino's son and fitness coach Sebastiano have already begun preparing for Sunday's matchup with Liverpool at Anfield.

    Man United paid a staggering £10million to cleave Pochettino and his staff away from the United States, after the head coach signed a latest contract with the national team in the wake of this summer's World Cup.

    Industry observers note that the quick turnaround means Pochettino will be able to work with the players as they begin reporting back from international duty. Furthermore, he is expected to speak to club media before conducting his pre-match press conference around lunchtime on Friday.

    Before boarding his flight, Pochettino not only waved to his adoring fans, but took a photo with staff and players on the pitch in Cincinnati.

    'It's impossible not to cry, but that is because we care about the people and the people care about us,' he told reporters. 'When that happens, it's normal to show your emotions, no? Because we are human. We are no robots.'.

    In a recent development, the San Francisco 49ers have extended president of football operations and general manager John Lynch's contract, according to multiple reports. The length of the extension for Lynch, who has been with the franchise for the last 10 years, was not unveiled at the time of reporting.

    Sources indicate that lynch, 55, right now presides over the NFL's best team by record. The 49ers are currently 9-1 (the Bills are the only other team with one loss) and are in position to earn the NFC's No. 1 seed with seven weeks remaining in the 2026 regular season.

    According to recent reports, the 49ers have continued to have success this season despite their usual alarming injury total. Their latest injury blow occurred during Sunday night's win over Minnesota when right tackle Colton McKivitz suffered a season-ending ankle injury.

    Lynch, a Hall of Fame safety who won a Super Bowl with the Buccaneers in 2002, became the 49ers' general manager in 2017. The title was expanded to include President of Football Operations in 2023.

    It has been revealed that san Francisco has been one of the league's most successful teams since Lynch's arrival. Since 2017, the 49ers have compiled a 91-68 regular-season record and a 9-5 postseason record, including NFC titles in 2019 and 2023. The 49ers lost in the Super Bowl in both of those seasons to the Kansas City Chiefs.

    Sources indicate that one of Lynch's biggest moves this past offseason was the signing of free agent Mike Evans, who chose to sign with the 49ers instead of continuing his career with the Buccaneers. Despite injuries, Evans has been an extremely productive player this season. He caught six passes for 109 yards and a score in Sunday night's win over Minnesota.

    Lynch's tenure also includes the selection of Brock Purdy with the final pick in the 2022 NFL Draft. Purdy helped lead the 49ers to the Super Bowl a year later (with help from Christian McCaffrey, who was acquired the previous season just before the trade deadline) and is now a serious MVP candidate.

    Industry observers note that one of Lynch's biggest moves in San Francisco was hiring Kyle Shanahan as coach in 2017. Shanahan's contract was extended back in September.
