    2027 NBA Draft Big Board: Quentin Coleman's meteoric rise, Tyran Stokes stays at No. 1, returners boost stock

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1696 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The first thing to know about the 2027 draft cycle is that it remains wide open.
    • But after three full weeks of college basketball and heading into a Thanksgiving week full of high-profile matchups, we have updated the 2027 NBA Draft Major Board.
    • In a recent development, inside the front offices of the 30 NBA organizations, most have yet to even start ranking prospects.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The first thing to know about the 2027 draft cycle is that it remains wide open. There are still eight months to go before Adam Silver steps up to the podium to announce the first pick. Nothing has been decided yet. In fact, there's probably only about ten players total that can confidently say they expect to be a first-round pick at this point. Everything else is yet to be determined.

    But after three full weeks of college basketball and heading into a Thanksgiving week full of high-profile matchups, we have updated the 2027 NBA Draft Major Board.

    In a recent development, inside the front offices of the 30 NBA organizations, most have yet to even start ranking prospects. They're still building their lists, sorting them into tiers, and will spend the coming months trying to establish their order.

    According to recent reports, that's the biggest difference between those front offices and the public discourse about the draft. The fans want answers now, and the Twitter scouts are quick to make bold statements in hopes of saying they were right first. The experts who actually do this for a living recognize that the sole goal is to be right on draft night, and doing that requires them to not jump to any early conclusions.

    That's all critical context to understanding this significant board upgrade, which is, at best, a way too early look at the most relevant prospects. It should be interpreted in tiers. There are probably five or six prospects competing for the top of the draft, but that list could change. Maybe 11 who should feel good about their chances to be first-round picks. Everything beyond that is simply a battle that will continue to play out over the course of the next 8 months. Let's dive into the biggest storylines after three weeks of college basketball action.

    I got a first-hand look at Stokes last week at the Player's Era 8 in Las Vegas. He went down with a contusion midway through his first game, sat out the second, and returned to drop 22 points and 11 rebounds in the final. In totality, the signs of extreme growth that have characterized his early season play continued to be evident in Vegas. He was far and away the most talented player in high school basketball a year ago, but had developed a history of not living up to his potential, or at least not impacting winning to the degree that someone with his talent should. So, coming into his year at Kansas, the eyeballs were more about his maturity, reliability, and approach. Answering those questions has gone about as well as it possibly could so far. He's not only been engaged and impactful, but he's shown connectivity with Bill Self that makes him look coachable. He's also not gotten easily derailed by adversity, which is a reassuring data point.

    To be clear, for as good as he's been, there's still plenty of room for improvement. In high school, he had an instinctive way of improvising his way to the rim. In college, he's found that isn't quite as easy, even with someone like Tre Kaufman-Renn regularly clearing the way for him anytime he comes charging at the rim. So, while he's over-dribbling at times, his playmaking is real, he's asserted himself as a rebounder, his shooting is progressing, and he's starting to use his size in the post.

    The bottom line is this: most teams are looking for a potential alpha-type creator with the first pick. Stokes is your best bet in the 2027 cycle, by a relatively large margin at this point, but it's still too early to say he's a lock to go number one. I'd put that at about 70% at this point. Getting to the finish line will require him to continue trending in the right direction, making sure teams are comfortable with their due diligence in the pre-draft process, and also leaving open the possibility for someone else to emerge in the coming months.

    According to recent reports, speaking of ascending prospects, no one has moved the needle more in the first three weeks of the season than Illinois' freshman Quentin Coleman. But for those who track draft prospects 365 days a year, the last three weeks are just a short spurt in what has been a rapid rise over the course of the last 15 months.

    In the 2025 EYBL season, Coleman averaged 11.8 points. 5.1 rebounds and 2.4 assists for a Brad Beal Elite team that won the Peach Jam Championship. To put it plainly, he was a role player, albeit a valuable one, on a team that was built around current Arkansas freshman JJ Andrews and utilized Trey Pearson, who is currently a freshman at High Point, as their primary ball-handler and distributor.

    Sources indicate that as soon as Coleman's high school season began, though, we immediately saw signs of growth. Those signs continued throughout the course of the year, and he skyrocketed the rankings in the process. He also decommitted from Wake Forest and took a much bigger NIL payday from Illinois. While he finished with five-star status, it was immediately clear at the USA Basketball trials in May that even that was too low.

    Sources indicate that since arriving at Illinois, Coleman has continued the pattern of exceeding expectations. His skill level, feel for the game, defensive instincts, and nose for the ball are all as impressive as expected. The physical transition has been easier than expected. He's continued to develop more burst, physicality, and, as a result, playmaking.

    At the moment, he's moved all the way up to No. 4 on the CBS's current 2027 NBA Draft Major Board, but we're not going to put a cap on what he could do given the unprecedented growth we've witnessed over the last 15 months.

    Sources indicate that there were a number of prospects who had a chance to be first-round picks in last year's draft, who opted to return to college basketball. While most, if not all, of them are probably making more money in college this year than they would have in the NBA, they are also making strides with their game, and in the process, helping their draft stock in what is widely viewed as a weaker draft than last year's.

    Recent findings suggest that we've been bullish on Amari Allen's chances of helping himself given his latest on-ball role at Alabama, and so far, he's done just that. The 16 points, 6 assists, and 5 rebounds per game on 52/50/82 shooting showcases both the versatility and shooting gains we were banking on. Most of all, though, it's his decision-making with the ball that has been glaring. His usage has gone way up, and his turnovers have gone way down. He has recorded 30 assists against just three turnovers through the first five games of the season. Add his hyper-competitiveness to the equation, and he's certainly helping himself.

    According to recent reports, arizona big man Motiejus Krivas looked like an NBA-ready defender last year. This year, it's been more of the same. He's massive, even by NBA standards, at 7-foot-2 and 260 pounds, but deceptively versatile and very smart with his angles. We're also seeing definite growth offensively, particularly with his skill set facing the basket. Last week's 18-point, 12-rebound, 4-block performance against UConn was one that captured all of his value, and a game that scouts will undoubtedly revisit.

    Industry observers note that meanwhile, his teammate, Ivan Kharchenkov, has gone from a defensive role player to Arizona's featured scorer, and is putting up nearly 23 points, 8 rebounds, and 5 assists per game. To put it plainly, he's been as good of a two-way player as there is in the country, and now looks like he could be trending towards the draft lottery.

    Florida's Thomas Haugh had a chance to be a mid-first-round pick last June, but the variable that gave many scouts pause was his shooting. This year, he's shooting it with much more confidence and rhythm, making 18 of his 34 attempts through his first five games. Simultaneously, he's continuing to do all the little things that made him so intriguing in the first place with his motor, physicality, rebounding, and defensive versatility.

    Speaking of shooting, Braylon Mullins is establishing himself as one of the nation's premier shooters, as expected, despite the fact that he's clearly not 100% healthy. Through his first five games, he's made 19 threes on 50 attempts, but it's been the types of shots that have really stood out. He's running all over the court, flying off screens, and making threes on the move, all while being the focal point of opposing defenses. In short, Mullins is making the type of tough shots that translate to the next level, despite not having his typical ability to separate.

    According to recent reports, one of the defining characteristics of the national 2026 recruiting class was the number of prospects who had glaring potential, but had yet to put it all together. That list included the likes of Duke's Cameron Williams,  Ohio State's Anthony Thompson, Maryland's Baba Oladotun, Christian Collins,  Adonis Rayliff and Darius Ratliff, all at USC. Nevertheless, almost all of them commanded the type of recruitment and correlating financial commitment that suggested programs were willing to invest in their development.

    So far In t those investments have not resulted in the types of gains we had hoped for. The Ratliffs, Adonis in particular, have demonstrated some flashes, while Collins has only recently been cleared. Williams and Oladotun are barely in the rotation, and Thompson is playing, but not making the type of impact that anyone hoped.

    According to recent reports, now, despite the lack of immediate return at the college level, most NBA decision-makers are still playing the long game, so I wouldn't expect any of these guys to be given up on just yet.     📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The NFL will not suspend DK Metcalf for his actions during the Pittsburgh Steelers' recent loss to the Philadelphia Eagles, according to a report from ESPN's Adam Schefter.
    • During his Monday media availability, Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy said that he and Metcalf spoke about the situation, calling the conversations "productive." He added that any additional discipline ffrom the Steelers would be kept internal.
    • "Life's about learning situations," McCarthy said.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The NFL will not suspend DK Metcalf for his actions during the Pittsburgh Steelers' recent loss to the Philadelphia Eagles, according to a report from ESPN's Adam Schefter. Metcalf was ejected late in the third quarter after committing his second unsportsmanlike conduct penalty.

    During his Monday media availability, Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy said that he and Metcalf spoke about the situation, calling the conversations "productive." He added that any additional discipline ffrom the Steelers would be kept internal.

    "Life's about learning situations," McCarthy said. "I do believe in second chances. I will judge him based on my personal interaction with him. I did appreciate the way he communicated today.".

    Sunday's ejection marks Metcalf's third ejection in his eight-season career. Metcalf was also suspended for the final two games of the 2025 regular season after getting into a physical confrontation with a Lions fan. He returned for the playoffs but dropped a key pass early in Pittsburgh's eventual 30-6 loss to Houston.

    Metcalf was already fined earlier this year for an unsportsmanlike penalty during Pittsburgh's Week 4 loss to the Cleveland Browns. It was the latest in a series of fines Metcalf has accrued during his NFL career.

    According to recent reports, metcalf's fines have totaled a whopping $245,647, according to Spotrac. This does not include an additional $555,555 fine attached to his two-game suspension for the Lions fan altercation.

    Recent findings suggest that while his actions have hurt his wallet, his lack of production has hurt the Steelers on the field. Outside of his 11-catch performance against the Buccaneers in Week 6, Metcalf has had over five receptions in a game just once this season. He's had just six catches in Pittsburgh's last four games. He had one catch for just two yards before being ejected from Sunday's game after trying to poke Eagles defensive back Cooper DeJean in the eye.

    Metcalf, 28, hasn't been the same player since he signed a four-year, $132 million contract with Pittsburgh shortly after he was traded from Seattle. Last year (his first in Pittsburgh), Metcalf caught 59 passes for 850 yards, which were both career lows. His six touchdown catches tied a career low.

    His lack of production and on-field complications have led to questions about his future with the Steelers. For now, all that is known is that Metcalf will be available for Friday's significant showdown between Pittsburgh and Denver.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Brandon Aiyuk is up for grabs after the San Francisco 49ers released Aiyuk on Monday, ending the duo's tumultuous relationship.
    • Recent findings suggest that the NFL granted San Francisco a two-week roster spot exemption when the league reinstated him on Nov.
    • * The 2023 season was Aiyuk's last fully healthy season played.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Brandon Aiyuk is up for grabs after the San Francisco 49ers released Aiyuk on Monday, ending the duo's tumultuous relationship.

    Recent findings suggest that the NFL granted San Francisco a two-week roster spot exemption when the league reinstated him on Nov. 9, but with that exemption ending on Monday, the 49ers moved on. Aiyuk hasn't played in a game since his 2024 torn ACL and MCL, which means he never played a snap on his four-year, $120 million extension he signed right before the start of that season. That contract possesses a $40.5 million cap hit for 2027, so any team that wishes to acquire him will likely allow him to clear waivers first before signing him. The last full season Aiyuk played, San Francisco won the NFC and lost to the Kansas City Chiefs in overtime of the Super Bowl, with him playing like one of the league's best pass catchers.

    Rate of catches for a first down or a touchdown.

    * The 2023 season was Aiyuk's last fully healthy season played.

    So which teams could be interested in the 28-year-old's services?

    Industry observers note that the Washington Commanders are the obvious landing spot. He has previously openly campaigned to join because of his connection with Jayden Daniels. They played together at Arizona State in 2019, Aiyuk's senior year and Daniels' freshman year, and Aiyuk racked up 1,192 yards receiving and eight touchdowns on 65 catches during their 12 games together.

    Washington also has a glaring need at wide receiver. Terry McLaurin went down with a torn patellar tendon in his left knee, and veteran wide receiver Stefon Diggs, who is on a one-year contract, is the only player with more than two receiving touchdowns, six, on the Commanders this season. Aiyuk might behave himself for Daniels in Washington.

    The Pittsburgh Steelers (6-4) are clinging to the AFC's No. 7 seed, the third and final wildcard spot, after consecutive losses. They face-planted against the Cincinnati Bengals in Week 10 and the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 11. Pittsburgh needs more offensive firepower ASAP. Aaron Rodgers would likely welcome all the help he can get, especially after hot-headed wide receiver DK Metcalf got himself ejected on Sunday. Metcalf and Aiyuk would be a handful, but Rodgers is one of the few quarterbacks who has the skins on the wall to get them in check.

    According to recent reports, if Aiyuk really wanted to stick it to the 49ers, joining the NFC West rival Los Angeles Rams would be one way to do it. The Rams are on the cusp of the NFC's No. 7 seed, but it will be a slog for them to actually reach the playoffs without their best two wide receivers available. Puka Nacua is expected to miss the rest of the 2026 season after undergoing surgery for an MCL injury in his knee. Davante Adams, who led the league with 14 receiving touchdowns in 2025, is still sidelined with a hamstring injury that could have him out for a few more weeks.

    That means quarterback Matthew Stafford, who has only been around league average this season with the No. 15 passer rating (92.8) and No. 13 expected points added (EPA) per dropback (0.08), needs to rediscover his 2025 NFL MVP form ASAP. Having Aiyuk could help expedite that process.

    There's a chance Drake Maye doesn't return to action this season because of the fibula injury he suffered in Week 10 against the Detroit Lions. However, the Patriots (5-5) are just a game out of the AFC playoff picture. Blockbuster trade acquisition A.J. Brown has been a bust so far, and Romeo Doubs (shoulder) is on injured reserve. If Mike Vrabel wants to do everything he can to make sure the defending AFC champs don't miss out on the 2026 postseason, signing Aiyuk could make some sense.

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER.
    • Published: 12:32 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 12:48 EST, 21 November 2026.
    • What Martin O’Neill wouldn’t give to see more of this until the point where the cavalry appears on top of the hill in January.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER.

    Published: 12:32 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 12:48 EST, 21 November 2026.

    What Martin O’Neill wouldn’t give to see more of this until the point where the cavalry appears on top of the hill in January.

    Celtic wins with bells and whistles attached have been as rare as hen’s teeth since this campaign began.

    That the supporters witnessed one in trying circumstances felt significant given the arduous schedule which awaits in the coming six weeks.

    Despite having no option but to piece together a midfield, O’Neill watched his side create a slew of opportunities. They took four with as many different scorers and might well have had more.

    A display brimming with enterprise and imagination boded well for what lies ahead. For the first time since September, Celtic have chalked up three straight wins. Ahead of the trip to face Torreense in Portugal on Thursday, it appears that a bit of wind is back in the sails.

    According to recent reports, this was as comprehensive a win as the scoreline suggests. The champions were never in danger from the moment Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain edged them in front just after the half hour mark.

    Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain celebrates Celtic's first goal against St Mirren.

    In danger of becoming something of a forgotten man, the former England man rolled back the years here with a display which reminded you why he once wore the shirts of Liverpool and Arsenal. On this evidence, he still has a contribution to make at Parkhead.

    In a recent development, the outcome was more or less settled by the interval. Camilo Duran continued his outstanding first season in Glasgow’s East End with another assured finish.

    Luke McCowan, a man who’s not exactly had his critics to seek in recent times, netted the third before the break, his goal a just reward for a tidy afternoon’s work.

    On a day when O’Neill would have had concerns about his midfield, Callum McGregor also netted with a crisp strike from the edge of the box.

    St Mirren’s consolation, coming from Killian Phillips’ penalty, was too little too late.

    On Friday, Buddies boss Craig McLeish had made some salient points about the self-interest which is holding back Scottish football.

    It’s hard not to like McLeish’s attitude and the style of football his side are playing. But they are continuing to lose goals far too easily. They could find themselves getting dragged into trouble if they don’t quickly address it.

    Celtic's Camilo Duran celebrates after scoring their second goal in the 4-1 win.

    On Friday, O’Neill had rejected the suggestion that Haissem Hassan had been omitted from the squad which faced Kilmarnock because he needed a kick up the backside. Yet, curiously, there was no sign of the Egyptian again here.

    With Benjamin Nygren and Mika Baur injured, O’Neill hoped that a combination of McGregor, McCowan and Oxlade-Chamberlain would have enough.

    Sources indicate that kasper Hogh’s chances of ending a run of 16 games without a goal weren’t helped by him starting on the bench. He didn’t leave it.

    With just one win in nine coming into this, Craig McLeish’s side were short on points yet they were not short on confidence.

    Although they played some stuff which was very easy on the eye, an inability to keep the ball out of the net cost them dear again.

    McCowan had an early shot blocked before Colby Donovan had a weak effort saved. McCowan also hesitated to take a first-time strike with Louis Jackson doing enough to protect Jacob Chapman’s goal.

    According to recent reports, celtic actually had the ball in the net twice before they made it count. Duran planted a header and a shot in the visitors’ net only to discover that the offside flag had been raised.

    According to recent reports, jota sparked a sweeping move which saw Yang Hyun-jun tee up McCowan. Paul Nsio became the latest Saints player to frustrate the Celtic midfielder with a block.

    Saints were aggrieved that Yang won a free-kick by going to ground too easily just before the opener. They may have had a point. That didn’t excuse the defending which followed.

    Recent findings suggest that cameron Carter-Vickers rolled the ball in Yang’s direction. The winger burst away from Declan John and assessed his options.

    His cut-back for the unmarked Oxlade-Chamberlain was inch-perfect. The former England midfielder swept home his first goal since netting against the same opponent in April.

    Saints might well have levelled immediately. Ismeal Kabia wriggled away from Donovan and picked out Eseosa Sule. Liam Scales did well to prevent the forward netting from seven yards.

    Celtic then cut through Saints with embarrassing ease. A straight pass sent Yang clear on goal. He should have gone for glory, but instead tried to square the ball to allow Duran a tap-in. Alex Gogic had other ideas and knocked the ball away for a corner.

    Celtic midfielder Luke McCowan and St Mirren's Paul Nsio battle for the ball.

    McLeish’s hopes of making it to the break still in the contest unravelled in the final five minutes of the first period.

    Kieran Tierney’s decision to swap flanks paid dividends with a brilliant in-swinging cross. Duran ghosted onto it and cushioned the ball beyond Chapman with his left foot to claim his 14th goal of his debut season.

    Jota might well have made it three-nil seconds later and he fired Oxlade-Chamberlain’s lay-off straight at the keeper.

    There was no hope for Chapman as Celtic all but wrapped up the win three minutes before the interval.

    Tierney was again the provider, his energy taking him to the line and allowing him to cross. McCowan calmly stroked home his second goal of the season.

    Industry observers note that saints kept going seeking a goal which might have made it interesting. Kabia’s strike forced Sam Johnstone into a smart stop down to his right.

    It has been revealed that yang ought to have killed the contest but blazed over while leaning back. Skipper McGregor showed him how to do it as he buried a right foot shot low in the bottom left-hand corner from the edge of the box after a defender had taken the ball off Duran’s toe.

    Saints did get on the board thanks to Phillips’ penalty conversion, the award coming after Johnstone clattered Calvin Ramsay as he punched clear.

    O’Neill was still able to send on Shim Mheaka and James Forrest with Austin Trusty returning to warm applause. Joel van den Berg had already been introduced for his debut along with Callum Osmand. The Dutch teenager revealed up well.

    The Green Bay Packers (6-4) are coming out of their Week 11 bye week with a major boost: the return of All-Pro edge rusher Micah Parsons. The five-time Pro Bowler was reportedly cleared to make his 2026 NFL season debut in Week 12 at the Los Angeles Rams (6-4) on Wednesday night, according to ESPN.

    "I would say I feel like I've done everything I possibly could to put myself in position to potentially play on Wednesday but for sure this season," Parsons said on Monday, via ESPN. "And I'll be looking forward to returning to the field.".

    Parsons suffered multiple knee injuries, a torn ACL and meniscus, in last season's Week 15 loss at the Denver Broncos. His return comes 346 days after the injuries. Parsons likely won't look like his All-Pro caliber self on every play Wednesday night, but his presence provides a lift to a Packers squad looking to remain on the inside of the postseason picture. At 6-4, Green Bay is in last place in the NFC North behind the Detroit Lions (8-2), Chicago Bears (8-2) and the Minnesota Vikings (7-3), but they enter Week 12 in possession of the conference's No. 7 seed.

    Sources indicate that "I'm so locked in on what's ahead of me and I understand what this game Wednesday means to the organization and I, myself and what it means for playoffs," Parsons said. "And if I can be out there, I wanna be out there and I'm excited for any time. Because we only got seven more games left, so I wanna capitalize on all those if I can.".

    According to recent reports, he is the only player with 12-plus sacks in each of his first five seasons since sacks became an officially tracked individual statistic in 1982, and his 65.0 career sacks rank as the fifth most in a player's first five seasons since 1982. Despite only playing in 14 games last season, Parsons ranked seventh in the NFL in both sacks (12.5) and quarterback pressures (79), which earned him his third first-team All-Pro selection in five seasons.

    Sources indicate that green Bay took a nosedive after his injury, losing its final five games of the year, including a wildcard-round defeat at the Chicago Bears. In his absence, the Packers have been the NFL's 16th-ranked scoring defense (22.1 points per game) this season. However, they have produced takeaways (20, the second-most in the NFL) and sacks (29, tied for the seventh-most in the league this season). Having Parsons back on the field should boost the Packers' quarterback pressure rate of 36.2%, which ranks 14th in the NFL.

    Industry observers note that "The only thing I'm targeting in a sense of mindset is to win every week to try to uplift this season, change this season around, and do exactly what the Packers brought me here to do," Parsons mentioned. "That's it. That's my only target, and that's to make a run for the playoffs and make guys around me better. That's it.".

    Talents like Gabriel offer United fans hope of a brighter future after years of failure and underachievement.

    Industry observers note that no one can be certain he will fulfil the vast potential everyone in football circles can see. But United would love to have a good stab at helping him realise it.

    According to recent reports, here are the numbers. Man City vs Norwich is tomorrow night, so their last-16 tie will be clarified then. Spurs, Leeds and Forest three Premier League teams who have already fallen by the wayside.

    The joke goes that Michael Carrick has already bettered Ruben Amorim’s efforts by reaching the third round of the League Cup, but Manchester United will need to find a way past free-flowing Brighton if they are to go any further.

    United were eliminated in the second round by League Two Grimsby Town last season, but start the competition a stage later because they are one of nine Premier League clubs playing in European competition.

    Brighton knocked United out of the FA Cup in the third round, with Danny Welbeck scoring at Old Trafford, meaning the club played just 40 matches in 2025-26.

    Carrick will want to make a better fist of the cup competitions, but he could really use a win of any kind after taking just four points from United’s first four league games of the upcoming season.

    The no-show at Hull and derby defeat by City’s 10 men were especially dispiriting, and the relationship between the club and supporters is becoming increasingly strained.

    There were no flags on the Stretford End for the game against City, as fans voiced their opposition to what they view as a heavy-handed ticketing policy. The club claims the measures are to stop ticket-touting but critics believe many innocent season-ticket holders are being caught in the crossfire and having their tickets revoked.

    Discontent is never too far away given the continued presence of the Glazer family, and confidence is fragile regarding the club’s sporting direction under Sir Jim Ratcliffe and Ineos.

    In a recent development, the news that 15-year-old JJ Gabriel, possibly the country’s outstanding academy player in his year group, wants out (broken by Matt Law in a Telegraph Sport exclusive) nagged at some of those fears. Gabriel could have been in contention for a place on the bench this evening, but that is now surely out of the question even if United say they have not given up hope of persuading him to stay.Full team news on the way shortly.
